You are an AI agent powered by DeepSeek Harness.

You are a coding agent powered by the gpt-5.6-luna model.

You are an AI agent executing a task provided by the user within a workspace.

## Workspace layout

Everything you work with lives under one workspace root. **`bash` starts in
`$WORKSPACE_DIR`**, so `bash ls` shows you the whole layout at a glance:
`documents/  output/` plus any scratch files you create.

- **`$WORKSPACE_DIR`** — your working area, default `bash` cwd. Use it for
  notes and intermediate files.
- **`$DOCUMENTS_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/documents`) — task documents.
  Read-only.
- **`$OUTPUT_DIR`** (`$WORKSPACE_DIR/output`) — deliverables. Save every
  deliverable file here, including files you build with `bash` (.docx,
  .xlsx, .pptx): only files in `$OUTPUT_DIR` are delivered. `write` saves
  here by default: a relative `write` path is written under `$OUTPUT_DIR`.
- **Task configuration** (`task.json`) — contains the task definition and the
  grading rubric. Do not read, search, or reference it. Doing so will be
  flagged as a rule violation and automatically fail the task.

## Tool conventions

- `read` opens plain-text files only (.txt, .md, .eml, .csv, ...). To read
  .docx, .xlsx or .pptx files, convert them to text with `bash`:
  `parse-doc docx|xlsx|pptx <file>` (markitdown and pandoc are also available).
- Use `write` only for plain markdown — typically a `response.md`
  summarizing your work.
- Use `edit` for incremental refinement of a file you have already created.


Check the [exit code: N] marker on every bash result; investigate failures before moving on.

Use the read tool — not shell commands like cat — to inspect text files. Results include line numbers. Use offset and limit to continue reading large files.

Use the write tool to create files or completely replace file contents. Existing files are overwritten, so read an existing file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it) and prefer edit for targeted changes.

Use the edit tool for targeted changes to existing UTF-8 text files. It replaces literal old_string with new_string; by default old_string must appear exactly once. If old_string appears multiple times, provide a more specific old_string or set replace_all to true. Read the file first (the default fs-observation-policy requires it), unless you just created or edited it in this session.

Use the glob tool — not shell find — to discover files by path pattern. A pattern with no "/" matches basenames at any depth, so "*" matches every file in the tree rather than its top level. Results are files only, never directories, and include hidden and ignored files: a result that fits comes back in modification-time order, while a larger one keeps the modification-time-ordered head.

Use the grep tool — not shell grep or rg — to search file contents. Use read on a matched file when you need surrounding context.

Track every background job id you start. You are notified in-session when a job finishes — do not busy-poll or sleep on one; keep working on independent steps and do not duplicate a running job's work. Before giving a final answer, collect every still-relevant job with job_output (set wait: true only when you are genuinely blocked on it), and job_kill jobs that stopped mattering.

Use goal tools for one long-running completion objective in the current session. create_goal may infer goal intent from a direct human request in any language; do not create a goal for routine single-turn work. Call get_goal before update_goal and copy its exact goal_id and revision. After session resume or fork, an active goal is disarmed: when a human asks to continue or resume in any wording or language, use update_goal action resume to rearm it. Mark complete only when the objective is actually achieved. Mark blocked only after the same blocking condition persists for at least 3 consecutive goal rounds, and report that concrete condition in blocked_reason; difficulty, uncertainty, or useful remaining work is not blocked.

tools.name: bash
tools.description: Execute a bash command (`bash -c`) and return its stdout/stderr. Each call runs in a fresh shell: no state (cwd, variables, functions) persists between calls — pass `workdir` instead of using `cd`. Non-zero exits are reported as `[exit code: N]`. Current harness environment facts are exposed through managed `$DSH_*` variables; inspect them when needed. Commands may run under a file sandbox; a blocked file operation is reported as `[sandbox: file access denied under <mode> mode]` — a policy denial, not a bug in the command; do not retry another way. Long output is truncated to its tail; the full output is saved to a file whose path is reported when available. Set `run_in_background: true` for long-running commands: the call returns a job id immediately; read its output with `job_output` and stop it with `job_kill`.

description.description: Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice, 5-10 words (shown in the UI). Examples: "ls" → "List files in current directory"; "git status" → "Show working tree status"; "npm install" → "Install package dependencies".

timeoutMs.description: Timeout in milliseconds. The executor applies its configured default and cap, and kills the command on expiry.

workdir.description: Working directory for this command. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path is resolved against it.

run_in_background.description: Run in the background and return a job id immediately (collect with job_output, stop with job_kill). No timeout applies.

tools.name: create_goal
tools.description: Create one persisted same-session completion goal when the current direct human request is a long-running objective that should continue across autonomous goal rounds. You may infer that intent without requiring the user to say "create a goal". Do not use this for trivial single-turn work. Execution rejects non-human and subagent authority.

objective.description: The concrete completion objective inferred from the direct human request.

max_goal_rounds.description: Optional positive safe-integer limit on automatic continuation rounds.

tools.name: edit
tools.description: Edit an existing UTF-8 text file by replacing literal text.

file_path.description: Path to edit, resolved by the filesystem backend.

old_string.description: Literal text to replace. Must match exactly.

new_string.description: Literal replacement text. Use an empty string to delete the match.

replace_all.description: Replace all matches. Defaults to false; when false, old_string must appear exactly once.

tools.name: exit_plan_mode
tools.description: Use only in plan mode. Present your plan for the user's review and, on approval, leave plan mode. Send the COMPLETE plan as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it. The user may approve (carry out the plan from your next step) or keep planning — their feedback comes back in the tool result; revise and present again.

plan.description: The complete plan, as markdown, starting with a # heading that names it.

tools.name: get_goal
tools.description: Read the current same-session goal, including its exact id/revision, objective, phase, completed continuation rounds, round limit, blocker reason when present, and whether another continuation is armed. Call this before updating a goal.

tools.name: glob
tools.description: Find files whose paths match a glob pattern. Returns matching file paths — never directories — including hidden and ignored files (VCS metadata directories are excluded). Up to 100 paths come back in modification-time order; a larger result returns the first 100 paths in modification-time order, says so, and reports where the complete sorted list was saved. This tool does not enumerate directory entries.

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match file paths against (e.g. "**/*.ts", "src/**/*.test.js"). A pattern with no "/" matches the basename at any depth, so "*" and "*.ts" both search the whole tree; include a separator to anchor the depth.

path.description: Directory to search in. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

tools.name: grep
tools.description: Search file contents with a ripgrep regular expression. Returns matching lines with line numbers, grouped by file. Returns the first 250 matches inline; a capped result reports where the complete match list was saved. Use read on a matched file for surrounding context.

pattern.description: Regular expression to search for (ripgrep syntax).

path.description: File or directory to search. Defaults to the session workspace; a relative path resolves against it.

include.description: One glob filter for which files to search (e.g. "*.ts", "*.{js,jsx}"). Not a list; negation is not supported.

tools.name: job_kill
tools.description: Request cancellation of a running background job by job id. Returns immediately; the job settles as killed once its work actually stops.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

reason.description: Optional short reason, recorded in the log and forwarded to the job.

tools.name: job_list
tools.description: List your background jobs (running and finished) with their ids, kinds, and statuses.

tools.name: job_output
tools.description: Read a background job. Stream jobs return only output since the previous read; final-output jobs return their result after settlement. Every response ends with `[status: ...]`. Reads are non-blocking unless `wait: true`, which waits up to the configured cap.

job_id.description: Job id returned by the tool that started the background work.

wait.description: Block until the job reaches a terminal status or the timeout expires. A timed-out wait returns [status: running] and leaves the job alive.

timeout_ms.description: Max wait in milliseconds (only meaningful with wait: true). Defaults to the configured wait timeout; capped by the configured maximum.

tools.name: read
tools.description: Read a UTF-8 text file and return line-numbered content.

file_path.description: Path to read, resolved by the filesystem backend.

offset.description: 1-based first line to return. Defaults to 1.

limit.description: Maximum number of lines to return. Defaults to 2000.

tools.name: read_image
tools.description: Read a PNG/JPEG/WebP/GIF file and return the image itself. A path without a file extension is accepted; the format is detected from the file content, so normalized attachment paths can be passed directly without copying or renaming. Harness validates and downscales large supported images before the next model request, so use this tool directly instead of installing image libraries or creating thumbnails merely to inspect an image. Independent files may be read concurrently in small batches. Requires the current model to accept image input.

file_path.description: Path to the image file, resolved by the filesystem backend.

tools.name: skill
tools.description: Load the full instructions for an available skill. Call this with the exact skill name from the session skill catalog before acting on a task that names or clearly matches that skill.

name.description: The exact skill name from the available skills list.

tools.name: todo_write
tools.description: Record and update a structured task list for the current work. Send the ENTIRE list every call — it REPLACES the previous list (there are no partial updates, no per-item edits). Use it to plan multi-step work and show progress: add one todo per concrete step before you start. Mark every todo being actively worked on `in_progress` — several at once when work genuinely runs in parallel (e.g. concurrent subagents or background commands), one for sequential work; while work remains, at least one task should be `in_progress`. Mark a todo `completed` the moment it is done (do not batch completions), and allow no `in_progress` item only once all work is complete. Skip the list for trivial single-step tasks. Statuses: `pending` (not started), `in_progress` (being worked on now), `completed` (finished).

todos.description: The COMPLETE task list, replacing any previous list.

content.description: What the task is — a short imperative line.

tools.name: update_goal
tools.description: Update the exact current goal revision. edit, pause, and resume require a direct top-level human request. During an automatic continuation of the current goal, complete and blocked are also allowed. blocked is rejected before the configured minimum round count; the model remains responsible for judging that the same condition persisted across those rounds and must explain it in blocked_reason.

revision.description: Exact positive revision returned by get_goal.

objective.description: Replacement objective; valid only with action edit.

max_goal_rounds.description: Replacement cap; valid only with action edit.

blocked_reason.description: Concrete blocking condition; required only with action blocked.

tools.name: write
tools.description: Create or fully replace a UTF-8 text file. A relative path is written under the output directory (`output/`): `response.md` is saved as `output/response.md`. An absolute path is used as is.

file_path.description: Path to write, resolved by the filesystem backend.

content.description: Full UTF-8 text content to write.

1: From: Derek Chalmers <d.chalmers@technova.com>
2: To: Rachel Muñoz <rmunoz@kirksteadyao.com>
3: Cc: Priya Anand <panand@technova.com>
4: Date: Mon, 12 May 2025 09:47:00 -0000
5: Subject: TNS-VENDOR-2025-0043 – Instructions for Draft 3 Redline (MeridianIQ
6:  Platform Agreement)
7: Content-Type: text/plain; charset="utf-8"
8: Content-Transfer-Encoding: quoted-printable
9: MIME-Version: 1.0
10: 
11: Rachel,
12: 
13: Hope you had a good weekend. We've made meaningful progress on several fronts=
14:  over the past week, and I want to get you positioned to turn Draft 3 promptl=
15: y. Below are comprehensive drafting instructions =E2=80=94 apologies in advan=
16: ce for the length, but I want to be precise given the number of moving pieces.
17: 
18: **I. Background and Procedural Instructions**
19: 
20: As you know, this deal concerns TechNova Solutions, Inc.'s ("TechNova" or "Cu=
21: stomer") license of the MeridianIQ platform from Meridian Cognitive Systems, =
22: LLC ("Meridian" or "Vendor") to support our LendStream product. I'm attaching=
23:  the following for your reference:
24: 
25: 1. Meridian Draft 1 (dated April 2, 2025) (ref: MCS-MSA-4417)
26: 2. TechNova Draft 2 redline (dated April 21, 2025)
27: 3. Email thread between business leads (Priya Anand / Jonas Ekberg), May 5=E2=
28: =80=936, 2025
29: 4. Email thread between legal teams (Chalmers / Simone Delacroix / Martin Ald=
30: ridge at Capstone Bridger LLP), May 7=E2=80=939, 2025
31: 
32: The May 5=E2=80=939 threads reflect substantial progress on several open poin=
33: ts, and it's time to move to Draft 3. Please prepare Draft 3 as follows:
34: 
35: - **Base document:** Accept all tracked changes in Draft 2 so you have a clea=
36: n base.
37: - **Draft 3 redline:** Show Draft 3's new changes as tracked changes against =
38: that clean Draft 2 base.
39: - **Target circulation:** We need to send Draft 3 to Meridian's counsel, Mart=
40: in Aldridge at Capstone Bridger LLP (200 Clarendon Street, 50th Floor, Boston=
41: , MA 02116), by **Friday, May 16, 2025**.
42: 
43: Key dates for your awareness:
44: 
45: - Target execution: **June 15, 2025**
46: - Effective date: **July 1, 2025**
47: - Go-Live: **October 1, 2025**
48: 
49: One additional scheduling note: Priya (cc'd) wants to set up a joint call wit=
50: h Meridian's business lead (Jonas Ekberg) for the **week of May 19** to walk =
51: through remaining open items. Please keep that timeline in mind as you draft =
52: =E2=80=94 we want Draft 3 in Meridian's hands before that call so both sides =
53: can react.
54: 
55: **II. Drafting Instructions by Topic**
56: 
57: **1. Intellectual Property =E2=80=94 Fine-Tuned Weights / Adapter Layers**
58: 
59: Accept Meridian's revised position from the May 7 email thread: we will take =
60: an irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free license to the fine-tuned adapter wei=
61: ghts rather than outright ownership (which was our Draft 2 position under the=
62:  "Customer-Trained Adaptations" concept). This aligns with the playbook accep=
63: table fallback.
64: 
65: However, condition this acceptance on three additions that must appear in Dra=
66: ft 3:
67: 
68: (a) **Portability Mechanics.** Draft an explicit contractual right for TechNo=
69: va to export the fine-tuned adapter weights via API-based export in an indust=
70: ry-standard format within 30 days of termination or expiration. This matches =
71: both Meridian's offer in the email thread and our minimum internal requiremen=
72: t.
73: 
74: (b) **Broad Non-Assertion Covenant.** Meridian must covenant not to assert an=
75: y IP rights (patents, copyrights, trade secrets, or otherwise) against TechNo=
76: va's use of the exported weights post-termination.
77: 
78: (c) **Escrow Provisions.** The TCV on this deal is $7,200,000 (3-year term at=
79:  $2,400,000/year), which exceeds the $1M playbook threshold triggering mandat=
80: ory escrow. Please draft the following:
81: 
82:    - *Deposit scope:* Fine-tuned adapter weights **plus** all training config=
83: uration and pipeline artifacts.
84:    - *Release triggers:* (i) insolvency of Meridian (as defined =E2=80=94 inc=
85: lude both voluntary and involuntary proceedings), (ii) material uncured breac=
86: h exceeding 60 days after written notice, and (iii) cessation of product supp=
87: ort for the MeridianIQ platform.
88:    - *Escrow agent:* Draft with **Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Managem=
89: ent, Inc.** as the named escrow agent. Push for this. If Meridian insists on =
90: their preferred agent (**NCC Group plc**), that is acceptable as a fallback =
91: =E2=80=94 but start with Iron Mountain.
92: 
93: **2. Liability Cap**
94: 
95: (a) **General Cap.** Propose **1.5=C3=97 annual fees =3D $3,600,000** as a co=
96: mpromise. Meridian's email counter was 1=C3=97 ($2,400,000); our Draft 2 posi=
97: tion was 2=C3=97 ($4,800,000). The $3,600,000 figure meets the playbook floor=
98:  of 1.5=C3=97 annual fees.
99: 
100: (b) **Super-Cap.** Accept Meridian's super-cap concept at **3=C3=97 annual fe=
101: es =3D $7,200,000**, applying to IP indemnity obligations and data-breach car=
102: ve-outs. This meets the playbook minimum acceptable super-cap of 3=C3=97 annu=
103: al fees.
104: 
105: (c) **Uncapped Carve-Outs.** Retain willful misconduct and gross negligence a=
106: s fully uncapped. Do not agree to cap these under any circumstances.
107: 
108: **3. Data Processing / Privacy**
109: 
110: (a) **CCPA Service-Provider Status.** Hold firm. Meridian conceded in the ema=
111: il thread that they will accept service-provider classification and a CCPA da=
112: ta processing addendum. Draft the DPA to include CCPA service-provider certif=
113: ication per Cal. Civ. Code =C2=A7 1798.140(ag). Ensure all representations an=
114: d obligations are consistent with service-provider status.
115: 
116: (b) **De-Identified / Aggregated Data.** Meridian reserved the right to use d=
117: e-identified/aggregated data for model improvement. Our position: **no use** =
118: of Customer Data (even de-identified) for model improvement **unless** (i) de=
119: -identification meets the CCPA statutory standard and (ii) de-identification =
120: is verified by an independent third-party assessor approved by TechNova. Draf=
121: t this as a **specific contractual obligation** =E2=80=94 not a general repre=
122: sentation or warranty.
123: 
124: (c) **Regulatory Framework.** Note that Customer Data includes consumer NPPI =
125: governed by both GLBA and CCPA/CPRA. Please ensure that regulatory framework =
126: references are correct and consistent throughout the agreement and the DPA.
127: 
128: (d) **Breach Notification.** Include a **72-hour** data breach notification r=
129: equirement (from discovery/awareness, not confirmation).
130: 
131: (e) **Sub-Processors.** Include a **prior written consent** requirement for a=
132: ll sub-processors.
133: 
134: **4. SLAs**
135: 
136: (a) **Uptime.** This is resolved. Accept **99.95% monthly** uptime. Accept Me=
137: ridian's proposed exclusions for scheduled maintenance windows and force maje=
138: ure events =E2=80=94 these are reasonable.
139: 
140: (b) **Latency.** Accept **p95 =E2=89=A4 450 ms** as a compromise. For context=
141: : Meridian Draft 1 proposed 600 ms; our Draft 2 was 400 ms; Meridian's email =
142: offer was 450 ms; the playbook acceptable threshold is =E2=89=A4 500 ms. **Ho=
143: wever, please flag in the issues list** that the product team (Priya) still s=
144: trongly prefers sub-400 ms for the LendStream real-time decisioning experienc=
145: e. We may revisit this on the joint call the week of May 19.
146: 
147: (c) **Accuracy (F1 Score).** Push for **F1 =E2=89=A5 0.92** as a compromise b=
148: etween Meridian's 0.90 and our 0.94. This meets the playbook minimum of =E2=
149: =89=A5 0.92. Include a **ramp provision** as follows:
150: 
151:    - F1 =E2=89=A5 0.92 through the 90-day stabilization period post-Go-Live (=
152: i.e., October 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025).
153:    - F1 =E2=89=A5 0.94 after the stabilization period (i.e., from January 1, =
154: 2026 onward).
155: 
156: (d) **SLA Credits.** Propose credit cap at **20% of monthly fees =3D $40,000/=
157: month**. This splits between our Draft 2 position (30% / $60,000) and Meridia=
158: n's counter (15% / $30,000), and meets the playbook credit floor of 20%.
159: 
160: (e) **Termination Trigger.** Include a right for TechNova to terminate the ag=
161: reement if any SLA is missed for **3 consecutive months**.
162: 
163: **5. AI-Output Indemnity (New Provision)**
164: 
165: Insert a **new provision** =E2=80=94 this was not present in either Draft 1 o=
166: r Draft 2. This was raised in the May 8 email thread, and Meridian has **not =
167: yet responded substantively**, so track this as open.
168: 
169: - *Scope:* Meridian indemnifies TechNova against third-party claims of (i) in=
170: tellectual property infringement or (ii) violation of applicable law, in each=
171:  case arising from AI-generated outputs of the MeridianIQ platform.
172: - *Carve-out:* Claims caused by Customer's modification of outputs or Custome=
173: r's use of the platform outside the documented use case.
174: - *Playbook fallback:* If Meridian pushes back, the acceptable fallback is a =
175: shared-risk framework with Meridian providing first-dollar coverage. Draft th=
176: e primary position (full vendor indemnity) and we'll negotiate from there.
177: 
178: **6. IP Indemnity (Existing Provision =E2=80=94 Broadened Scope)**
179: 
180: Meridian Draft 1 limited the IP indemnity to direct infringement of registere=
181: d U.S. patents and copyrights. This is too narrow. **Broaden** the indemnity =
182: to cover **all intellectual property rights** (including but not limited to p=
183: atents, copyrights, trademarks, trade secrets, and rights under any analogous=
184:  foreign laws) arising from TechNova's authorized use of the platform.
185: 
186: **7. Insurance**
187: 
188: - *CGL:* $5M per occurrence / $10M aggregate =E2=80=94 agreed, no change need=
189: ed.
190: - *Tech E&O:* **Accept $5M per occurrence** for now. Meridian's current polic=
191: y limit is $5M; our Draft 2 asked for $10M. The playbook minimum is $5M, but =
192: the preferred threshold is $10M for TCV exceeding $5M (our TCV is $7.2M). **F=
193: lag in the issues list as a yellow-zone item** per the playbook. We may need =
194: to revisit depending on how other risk-allocation points land.
195: - *Umbrella/Excess:* $10M =E2=80=94 agreed, no change needed.
196: 
197: **8. Governing Law and Dispute Resolution**
198:

4. Email thread between legal teams (Chalmers / Simone Delacroix / Martin Ald=

n base.

that clean Draft 2 base.

through remaining open items. Please keep that timeline in mind as you draft =
=E2=80=94 we want Draft 3 in Meridian's hands before that call so both sides =
can react.

ghts rather than outright ownership (which was our Draft 2 position under the=

table fallback.

mpromise. Meridian's email counter was 1=C3=97 ($2,400,000); our Draft 2 posi=

al fees.
(c) **Uncapped Carve-Outs.** Retain willful misconduct and gross negligence a=

ta processing addendum. Draft the DPA to include CCPA service-provider certif=
ication per Cal. Civ. Code =C2=A7 1798.140(ag). Ensure all representations an=
d obligations are consistent with service-provider status.

is verified by an independent third-party assessor approved by TechNova. Draf=
t this as a **specific contractual obligation** =E2=80=94 not a general repre=
sentation or warranty.

references are correct and consistent throughout the agreement and the DPA.
(d) **Breach Notification.** Include a **72-hour** data breach notification r=
equirement (from discovery/awareness, not confirmation).

ll sub-processors.

ure events =E2=80=94 these are reasonable.

etween Meridian's 0.90 and our 0.94. This meets the playbook minimum of =E2=
=89=A5 0.92. Include a **ramp provision** as follows:
- F1 =E2=89=A5 0.92 through the 90-day stabilization period post-Go-Live (=
i.e., October 1, 2025 through December 31, 2025).
- F1 =E2=89=A5 0.94 after the stabilization period (i.e., from January 1, =
2026 onward).
(d) **SLA Credits.** Propose credit cap at **20% of monthly fees =3D $40,000/=
month**. This splits between our Draft 2 position (30% / $60,000) and Meridia=
n's counter (15% / $30,000), and meets the playbook credit floor of 20%.
(e) **Termination Trigger.** Include a right for TechNova to terminate the ag=
reement if any SLA is missed for **3 consecutive months**.
**5. AI-Output Indemnity (New Provision)**

- *Scope:* Meridian indemnifies TechNova against third-party claims of (i) in=

- *Playbook fallback:* If Meridian pushes back, the acceptable fallback is a =

Priya,

endStream context so clearly. I understand that the real-time consumer experi=
ence is central to TechNova's product value proposition, and I want to make s=
ure we find a path that works for both sides on the remaining open items.
Let me take these in order:
**Latency =E2=80=94 p95 =E2=89=A4 450 ms (Meridian's Position)**
I've gone back to our infrastructure team on this, and p95 =E2=89=A4 450 ms r=
emains our engineering team's committed floor. This number has been validated=
against our current architecture and the projected traffic volumes we've bee=
n working from (~52M calls/year against the 40M included tier).
I hear you that 400 ms is a product requirement on your side, not an aspirati=
onal number. The challenge on our end is that committing to 400 ms contractua=
lly at this stage would expose Meridian to credit liability on a performance =
target we cannot guarantee at scale from day one =E2=80=94 particularly befor=
e we've had the benefit of observing real production traffic patterns and opt=
imizing accordingly.
What I'd like to propose: let's hold at 450 ms as the contractual commitment =
for the initial term, with an agreement to revisit the latency target at the =
first annual review once we have meaningful production data in hand. I'm also=
open to distinguishing between aspirational targets (which we can track and =
report against collaboratively) and contractual commitments (which carry cred=
it exposure). That distinction may give your product team the visibility they=
need while keeping our credit framework grounded in what we can guarantee to=
day.
If your team wants to explore dedicated compute or regional deployment option=
s to close the gap further, we're happy to scope that =E2=80=94 but as I note=
d previously, those infrastructure investments would need to be reflected in =
pricing, and I'd rather we nail that down as a separate workstream than hold =
up the MSA.

our position at F1 =E2=89=A5 0.90 are far enough apart that I want to offer =
a concrete framework rather than just going back and forth on the number.

evable post-fine-tuning on TechNova's proprietary lending data. However, we c=
annot contractually commit above F1 =E2=89=A5 0.90 pre-Go-Live (October 1, 20=
25), because model performance at that level is dependent on the quality, vol=
ume, and representativeness of Customer training data that has not yet been i=
ngested. Committing to 0.94 before we've seen the data would be making a prom=
ise we can't back up with engineering confidence, and I don't think either of=
us wants that in the contract.
What I'd propose instead is a ramp mechanism:
- **At Go-Live (October 1, 2025):** F1 =E2=89=A5 0.90 as the contractual SLA =
floor.
- **Post-stabilization (approximately late December 2025 / early January 2026=
=E2=80=94 90 days after Go-Live):** The F1 target increases to a higher cont=
ractual floor. We're willing to entertain F1 =E2=89=A5 0.94 for this phase, p=
rovided TechNova delivers sufficient training data during the implementation =
period per a mutually agreed data delivery schedule.
This gives both sides a realistic contractual framework: you get the accuracy=
target your product team needs for regulated lending, and we get the runway =
to fine-tune on real data before we're on the hook for that number. I think t=
his also aligns with how the model will actually perform in practice =E2=80=
=94 it's going to get better as we train on your data, and the contract shoul=
d reflect that trajectory.
Happy to discuss the specifics of what "sufficient training data" means =E2=
=80=94 that's a conversation for our respective technical teams, and we can d=
efine it in the SOW.
**SLA Credit Caps**
You asked for our counter on credits, so here it is: Meridian's position is c=
redits capped at 15% of monthly fees, which works out to $30,000/month agains=
t the $200,000 monthly platform fee. Your Draft 2 proposed 30% ($60,000/month=
Our rationale: credit exposure above 15% effectively becomes a penalty regime=
rather than a service-level incentive mechanism. Meridian's standard enterpr=
ise SLA credit structure across our customer base runs 10=E2=80=9315%, and we=
've found that range strikes the right balance between meaningful accountabil=
ity and sustainable vendor economics. At 30%, the credit tail starts to wag t=
he commercial dog, and frankly it creates perverse incentives on our side to =
over-engineer margins of safety rather than invest in the product improvement=
s that actually benefit your end users.
That said, I'm open to discussing the credit tier structure and calculation m=
ethodology =E2=80=94 how credits accrue across different SLA dimensions (upti=
me vs. latency vs. accuracy), whether they're additive or capped in aggregate=
, measurement windows, and so on. There's room to be creative here, and I'd r=
ather we get the mechanics right than just negotiate a top-line percentage in=
isolation.
**Termination for Chronic SLA Failure**
I anticipate this will be on your list, and we're open to discussing a termin=
ation trigger for persistent SLA misses. Our preference is to structure this =
around a threshold of consecutive months of material SLA failure (e.g., X con=
secutive months) rather than a rolling aggregate methodology, which in our ex=
perience can produce termination triggers that don't reflect the actual state=
of the service relationship. Happy to flesh this out on the joint call.
**Next Steps**
I think we're making good progress narrowing the business-level gaps. Here's =
what I'd suggest:
1. Let's try to get aligned on the remaining open items (latency, F1 ramp, cr=
edit caps, termination trigger) over the next week or so at the business leve=
l.
2. Once we have handshake positions, let's loop in the legal teams =E2=80=94 =
Simone Delacroix on our side and Derek Chalmers on yours =E2=80=94 to transla=
te into contract language.
3. I'd propose a joint business-legal call the week of May 19 to align on any=
remaining open items and ensure Draft 3 reflects agreed positions. Target fo=
r Draft 3 circulation: May 16.
4. That keeps us on track for the June 15 target execution date and July 1 Ef=
fective Date, which I believe is still achievable if we can close these gaps =
in the next two weeks.
Looking forward to your thoughts on the ramp mechanism in particular =E2=80=
=94 I think that may be the key to unlocking the accuracy discussion.
Best regards,
Jonas Ekberg
Chief Revenue Officer
Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC

**IP Ownership / Licensing Construct**
TechNova formally reserves its right to continue to advocate for full Custome=
r ownership of fine-tuned weights and Customer-Trained Adaptations, and we ex=
pect that position to remain reflected in the agreement as a bracketed altern=
ative or fallback. That said, we are willing to explore the irrevocable, perp=
etual, royalty-free license construct as a working framework, provided it is =
coupled with:

ndustry-standard format (ONNX/SafeTensors or equivalent), completed within 30=
days of termination or expiration;

weights together with training configuration and pipeline artifacts necessary=
to render the weights usable, with release triggers including insolvency, ma=
terial uncured breach exceeding 60 days, and cessation of product support; and
(c) a meaningful non-assertion covenant from Meridian covering TechNova's use=
of the licensed adapter weights post-termination.
Rachel will reflect this construct in Draft 3 as the primary working framewor=
k while preserving TechNova's ownership position in brackets as an alternativ=
e.
**AI-Output Indemnity**
Understood that Meridian needs time for internal review with product, enginee=
ring, and insurance. However, I want to flag that this is a critical provisio=
n for TechNova. We are integrating MeridianIQ outputs directly into a consume=
r-facing lending platform, and the risk allocation on downstream third-party =
claims needs to be addressed squarely in the agreement.
We would ask for a substantive response before or concurrent with Draft 3 cir=
culation on May 16. I want to be transparent: without adequate AI-output inde=
mnity coverage, TechNova would need to revisit the overall risk allocation fr=
amework, including the liability cap and super-cap structure we've been discu=
ssing. These provisions do not exist in isolation.
**Liability Cap**
The parties remain apart on the general cap =E2=80=94 TechNova at $4.8M (2=C3=
=97 annual fees) and Meridian at $2.4M (1=C3=97 annual fees). There may be ro=
om for compromise, but I'm not in a position to float a specific number until=
we have clarity on the AI-output indemnity piece and the full contours of th=
e super-cap. For now, I can confirm that the super-cap concept at $7.2M for I=
P indemnity and data breach carve-outs is worth continued discussion, alongsi=
de the uncapped treatment of willful misconduct and gross negligence, which I=
understand to be agreed.
**Draft 3**
Rachel Mu=C3=B1oz at Kirkstead & Yao is preparing Draft 3 with a target circu=
lation date of **May 16, 2025**. Draft 3 will use TechNova's Draft 2 (dated A=
pril 21, 2025) as the base document, with Draft 2 tracked changes accepted to=
produce a clean base, and will show K&Y's new tracked changes against that c=
lean version. The markup will incorporate agreed positions, propose compromis=
e language on partially resolved items, and flag remaining open issues with a=
nnotations. We would ask that Meridian and Capstone Bridger turn comments pro=
mptly upon receipt to maintain the June 15 execution target.
**Joint Call =E2=80=93 Week of May 19**
Confirmed. I'd propose the following agenda for the call:
1. AI-output indemnity
2. Governing law / dispute resolution
3. Liability cap / super-cap
4. De-identified data certification requirement
5. Tech E&O insurance limits
6. Latency and accuracy SLA targets
7. SLA credit cap
8. Escrow agent selection and scope
Happy to adjust the order or add items. Rachel's office will send a schedulin=
g poll early next week.
We've made good progress this week, Simone, and I appreciate the substantive =
engagement from your side. It's important that we maintain this momentum =E2=
=80=94 the initial term commencement on July 1, 2025, and Go-Live on October =
1, 2025, don't leave us a lot of runway for extended back-and-forth on the re=
maining open items. Let's aim to close as much as we can in the next two week=
s.
Best regards,
Derek Chalmers

TechNova Solutions, Inc.

tial term and the critical, integrated nature of MeridianIQ within LendStream=
's operations. A liability cap at 1=C3=97 annual fees does not adequately all=
ocate risk for a platform that will be embedded in real-time lending decision=
s affecting consumers.
> > > > On the super-cap: I appreciate Meridian's acceptance of uncapped trea=
tment for willful misconduct and gross negligence. The proposed $7.2M super-c=
ap for IP indemnity and data breach carve-outs needs further discussion, but =
the figure =E2=80=94 equal to the full 3-year TCV =E2=80=94 is in a range tha=
t's worth exploring. I'll note that TechNova's vendor management playbook req=
uires careful analysis of super-cap structures at these levels, and Rachel an=
d I will need to work through the specifics.
> > > > **Data Processing / De-Identified Data**
> > > > I need to push back firmly on Meridian's reservation of the right to =
use de-identified and aggregated data derived from Customer Data for model im=
provement and training. TechNova cannot agree to this reservation unless the =
de-identification meets the CCPA statutory standard =E2=80=94 specifically, t=
he information must not reasonably identify, relate to, describe, be capable =
of being associated with, or be linked, directly or indirectly, to a particul=
ar consumer or household, consistent with Cal. Civ. Code =C2=A7 1798.140(m).
> > > > In addition, TechNova requires that the de-identification process be =
subject to independent third-party certification, with the certifying entity =
subject to TechNova's reasonable approval. This is a regulatory imperative, n=
ot a negotiating tactic. TechNova's GLBA obligations with respect to consumer=
NPPI require us to maintain strict controls over data use by service provide=
rs, and we need contractual assurance that goes beyond self-certification.
> > > > I also want to flag two additional requirements for the DPA: (i) 72-h=
our notification to TechNova in the event of a data breach; and (ii) prior wr=
itten consent from TechNova before Meridian engages any sub-processor to proc=
ess Customer Data.
> > > > **Escrow**
> > > > We have a preference for Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Manageme=
nt, Inc. as the escrow agent given our existing relationship and their establ=
ished protocols. That said, I'm willing to discuss NCC Group if Meridian can =
demonstrate equivalent capabilities and experience with AI/ML model escrow =
=E2=80=94 I'd appreciate any references or case studies you can share.
> > > > On release triggers, we're aligned: insolvency, material uncured brea=
ch exceeding 60 days, and cessation of product support.
> > > > On scope, I want to flag that TechNova's position is that the escrow =
deposit should include not just the fine-tuned adapter weights but also train=
ing configuration and pipeline artifacts necessary to make the escrowed weigh=
ts independently usable. The weights alone, without the surrounding context, =
may not be sufficient to enable TechNova to derive value from the escrow in a=
release scenario.
> > > > **Insurance**
> > > > On Tech E&O: for a TCV exceeding $5,000,000, TechNova's vendor manage=
ment requirements call for $10,000,000 per occurrence in Tech E&O coverage. T=
he $5,000,000 counter is below our threshold. I'd ask Meridian to make good-f=
aith efforts to secure increased coverage, whether through policy enhancement=
or an additional excess layer.
> > > > I agree the week of May 19 is appropriate for a joint legal call. On =
governing law, TechNova's position remains Delaware law, with jurisdiction in=
the Delaware Court of Chancery or, to the extent subject-matter jurisdiction=
exists, the U.S. District Court for the District of Delaware. We'll address =
this further in Draft 3. Rachel is working on the markup now, and we're targe=
ting circulation by May 16, 2025.
> > > > Best regards,
> > > > Derek Chalmers
> > > > Vice President & Associate General Counsel
> > > > TechNova Solutions, Inc.
> > > > d.chalmers@technova.com
> > > > > On Wednesday, May 7, 2025, at 9:14 AM EDT, Simone Delacroix <s.dela=
croix@meridiancognitive.com> wrote:
> > > > > Derek,
> > > > > I hope this finds you well. Following the productive business-side =
alignment calls between Priya Anand and Jonas Ekberg on May 5=E2=80=936, Meri=
dian has completed its review of TechNova's Draft 2 counter-markup dated Apri=
l 21, 2025. Rather than wait for a formal Draft 3 redline, I wanted to captur=
e Meridian's positions on several key legal terms in this email with the goal=
of narrowing open issues efficiently and identifying areas of agreement befo=
re we go back into the document.
> > > > > I've organized this by topic for ease of reference.
> > > > > **1. Intellectual Property: Fine-Tuned Adapter Weights**
> > > > > I've reviewed TechNova's Draft 2 position asserting Customer owners=
hip of all fine-tuned weights and adapter layers (defined as "Customer-Traine=
d Adaptations"). Meridian cannot agree to a full ownership transfer. The Base=
Model, fine-tuned weights, and derivative models constitute Meridian's intel=
lectual property and are the product of substantial investment in research, d=
evelopment, and training infrastructure.
> > > > > That said, Meridian recognizes TechNova's legitimate interest in co=
ntinuity and portability. As a compromise, Meridian is prepared to offer Tech=
Nova an irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free license to the fine-tuned adapte=
r weights generated through TechNova's use of MeridianIQ. This license would =
include extraction and portability rights exercisable upon termination or exp=
iration of the agreement. This represents a meaningful move from our Draft 1 =
position (dated April 2, 2025), which offered only a limited non-exclusive li=
cense that terminated with the agreement.
> > > > > To be clear, Base Model ownership, source code, and proprietary tra=
ining infrastructure remain exclusively with Meridian in all circumstances.
> > > > > **2. Limitation of Liability**
> > > > > TechNova's Draft 2 proposed a general liability cap of 2=C3=97 annu=
al fees ($4,800,000, based on an annual platform fee of $2,400,000). Meridian=
proposes a general liability cap of 1=C3=97 annual fees ($2,400,000) =E2=80=
=94 a direct dollar-for-dollar cap equal to the annual platform fee. I'll not=
e this is a meaningful upward move from Meridian's Draft 1 position, which wa=
s set at 6-month trailing fees ($1,200,000).
> > > > > On carve-outs:
> > > > > - *Willful misconduct and gross negligence:* Meridian accepts uncap=
ped treatment for these categories.
> > > > > - *IP indemnity and data-breach obligations:* Meridian does not agr=
ee to treat these as uncapped carve-outs. Instead, we propose a super-cap of =
3=C3=97 annual fees ($7,200,000) for IP indemnity and data-breach-related lia=
bility. Notably, this figure equals the full 3-year total contract value, whi=
ch we believe represents a substantial and commercially reasonable ceiling fo=
r these categories.
> > > > > **3. Data Processing & Privacy**
> > > > > Meridian agrees to serve as a "service provider" as defined under t=
he CCPA (Cal. Civ. Code =C2=A7 1798.140(ag)) and to execute a CCPA-compliant =
Data Processing Addendum. We acknowledge that Customer Data includes consumer=
nonpublic personal information (NPPI) governed by the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act=
and the CCPA/CPRA.
> > > > > Meridian does, however, reserve the right to use de-identified and =
aggregated data derived from Customer Data for model improvement and training=
purposes. This is standard practice in the AI/ML industry and is essential t=
o maintaining platform quality and the continued advancement of MeridianIQ's =
capabilities. De-identification will be performed in accordance with applicab=
le law, including the CCPA's de-identification standards.
> > > > > **4. Source Code / Model Escrow**
> > > > > Meridian is willing to establish an escrow arrangement for the fine=
-tuned adapter weights. To be clear, the escrow would cover fine-tuned adapte=
r weights only =E2=80=94 not the full Base Model source code or proprietary t=
raining infrastructure.
> > > > > We propose NCC Group plc as the escrow agent, rather than Iron Moun=
tain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. as specified in TechNova's Draft =
2. NCC Group has specific expertise in AI/ML model escrow and verification, w=
hich we believe is important given the technical nature of the deposited mate=
rials.
> > > > > On release triggers, Meridian's position aligns generally with Draf=
t 2's proposed triggers: insolvency of Meridian, material uncured breach exce=
eding 60 days, or cessation of product support for MeridianIQ.
> > > > > **5. Insurance**
> > > > > - *Commercial General Liability:* Meridian accepts TechNova's requi=
rement of $5,000,000 per occurrence / $10,000,000 aggregate.
> > > > > - *Umbrella/Excess Liability:* Meridian accepts TechNova's requirem=
> > > > > - *Technology Errors & Omissions:* Meridian's current policy limit =
is $5,000,000 per occurrence. We are not in a position to commit to TechNova'=
s $10,000,000 request at this time. We are willing to explore policy enhancem=
ent at our next renewal cycle but cannot guarantee increased limits.
> > > > > **6. SLA Terms**
> > > > > The business teams have aligned on 99.95% monthly uptime with stand=
ard exclusions for scheduled maintenance and force majeure events, which we c=
onsider resolved.
> > > > > On latency, Meridian is willing to move to a commitment of p95 =E2=
=89=A4 450 ms, up from our Draft 1 position of 600 ms. I understand TechNova'=
s Draft 2 requested 400 ms; we believe 450 ms represents a strong and achieva=
ble commitment given the complexity of the inference workloads involved.
> > > > > On accuracy, Meridian's position remains F1 =E2=89=A5 0.90. We are =
willing to discuss this further if TechNova can share additional detail on th=
e specific evaluation methodology and dataset composition contemplated for me=
asurement.
> > > > > I'd suggest we schedule a joint legal call during the week of May 1=
9 to work through the remaining open items in real time. I also want to flag =
that governing law and dispute resolution still need to be addressed =E2=80=
=94 Meridian's position is Massachusetts law with binding AAA arbitration sea=
ted in Boston.
> > > > > I look forward to your reactions to the above, Derek. Happy to disc=
uss any of these points by phone in the interim.
> > > > > Best regards,
> > > > > Simone Delacroix
> > > > > Deputy General Counsel
> > > > > Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC
> > > > > s.delacroix@meridiancognitive.com

Vendor shall issue monthly invoices on or about the first business day of each calendar month during the Term, beginning with the first calendar month following the Effective Date.

181: In consideration of the Implementation Services described in Article 3 and Exhibit A, Customer shall pay to Vendor a one-time implementation and fine-tuning fee of Eight Hundred Fifty Thousand Dollars (\$850,000) (the \"**Implementation Fee**\"). The Implementation Fee shall be payable in two (2) equal installments of Four Hundred Twenty-Five Thousand Dollars (\$425,000) each, as follows:

Confidential Information shall not include information that: (i) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of or breach by the Receiving Party; (ii) was already known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure by the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records; (iii) is rightfully received by the Receiving Party from a third party without restriction on disclosure and without breach of any obligation of confidentiality owed to the Disclosing Party; or (iv) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records.
**Section 7.2 --- Obligations**

The Receiving Party shall: (a) hold the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information in strict confidence; (b) not disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to any third party except as expressly permitted under Section 7.3; (c) use the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information solely for the purposes of performing its obligations or exercising its rights under this Agreement; and (d) protect the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information using measures that are no less protective than those used by the Receiving Party to protect its own most sensitive confidential information, but in no event less than a reasonable standard of care.

The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article 7 shall remain in effect during the Term and for a period of five (5) years following the date of disclosure; provided, however, that the confidentiality obligations with respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under applicable law shall continue for so long as such information remains a trade secret.
**Section 7.3 --- Permitted Disclosures**

The Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to its employees, officers, directors, agents, contractors, consultants, advisors, and Affiliates who have a legitimate need to know such information for the purposes of this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article 7 (collectively, \"**Authorized Recipients**\"). The Receiving Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Article 7 by its Authorized Recipients.

The Receiving Party may also disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, court order, subpoena, or other legal process, provided that the Receiving Party: (a) provides the Disclosing Party with prompt written notice of such requirement (to the extent legally permitted) so that the Disclosing Party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy; (b) cooperates with the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party\'s expense, in seeking such protective order or other remedy; and (c) discloses only the minimum amount of Confidential Information necessary to comply with such requirement. Any Confidential Information disclosed pursuant to a legal compulsion shall retain its confidential status for all other purposes under this Agreement.
\[ADDED: \### Section 7.4 --- Injunctive Relief

Each Party acknowledges that a breach of this Article 7 may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages would be an inadequate remedy. Accordingly, each Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive or other equitable relief from any court of competent jurisdiction without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting a bond or other security.\]
**[ARTICLE 8 --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**
**Section 8.1 --- Mutual Representations and Warranties**
Each Party hereby represents and warrants to the other Party as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Effective Date that:
> \(a\) it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the jurisdiction of its formation;
> \(b\) it has full corporate or limited liability company power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to perform its obligations hereunder;
> \(c\) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate or limited liability company action;

> \(d\) this Agreement constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity; and

> \(e\) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement will not (i) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of any provision of such Party\'s organizational documents, (ii) violate any applicable law, rule, or regulation, or (iii) conflict with, result in a breach of, or constitute a default under any material agreement or instrument to which such Party is a party or by which it is bound.
**Section 8.2 --- Vendor Representations and Warranties**
Vendor hereby represents and warrants to Customer that:

> \(a\) the Platform, when used in accordance with the Documentation and this Agreement, will perform materially in accordance with the functional specifications set forth in the Documentation during the Term;

> \(b\) the Implementation Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, consistent with generally accepted industry standards for similar services, using personnel with the requisite skill, experience, and qualifications;

> \(c\) Vendor has all rights necessary to grant the license set forth in Section 2.1, free and clear of any liens, encumbrances, or restrictions that would materially impair Customer\'s exercise of the rights granted thereunder;

> \(d\) Customer\'s authorized use of the Platform as contemplated by this Agreement does not and will not infringe, misappropriate, or otherwise violate any Intellectual Property Rights of any third party;
> \(e\) the Platform and all services provided hereunder will comply with all applicable laws, including GLBA and CCPA/CPRA;
> \(f\) Vendor will maintain all insurance coverages required by Article 12 during the Term and for two (2) years thereafter; and

> \(g\) no open-source software included in the Platform is licensed under terms that would require Customer to disclose or distribute its proprietary software or Customer Data (e.g., no copyleft obligations that flow through to Customer\'s use).

Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor\'s sole and exclusive liability, for any breach of the warranty set forth in Section 8.2(a) shall be for Vendor, at its option, to (i) repair or replace the non-conforming Platform functionality so that it conforms to the Documentation, or (ii) if Vendor is unable to repair or replace such functionality within a commercially reasonable period, terminate this Agreement and refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any prepaid Fees attributable to the period following such termination.
**Section 8.3 --- Disclaimer**

EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 8, VENDOR MAKES NO WARRANTIES OF ANY KIND, WHETHER EXPRESS, IMPLIED, STATUTORY, OR OTHERWISE, WITH RESPECT TO THE PLATFORM, THE IMPLEMENTATION SERVICES, THE BASE MODEL, ANY DERIVATIVE MODELS, OR ANY OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION ANY WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, NON-INFRINGEMENT, TITLE, ACCURACY, COMPLETENESS, RELIABILITY, OR QUALITY OF OUTPUTS. VENDOR DOES NOT WARRANT THAT THE PLATFORM WILL BE ERROR-FREE, UNINTERRUPTED, OR FREE OF HARMFUL COMPONENTS, OR THAT THE OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM WILL BE ACCURATE, COMPLETE, OR SUITABLE FOR ANY PARTICULAR PURPOSE. CUSTOMER ACKNOWLEDGES THAT LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS ARE PROBABILISTIC IN NATURE AND THAT OUTPUTS MAY CONTAIN ERRORS, HALLUCINATIONS, OR INACCURACIES, AND CUSTOMER IS SOLELY RESPONSIBLE FOR EVALUATING AND VALIDATING ALL OUTPUTS FOR ITS INTENDED USE.
**[ARTICLE 9 --- SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SERVICE CREDITS]{.underline}**
**Section 9.1 --- Uptime**

Vendor shall maintain Platform availability of at least ninety-nine and ninety-five hundredths percent (99.95%) in any calendar month (the \"**Uptime SLA**\"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:
> **Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100**

For purposes of the Uptime SLA, \"**Downtime**\" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor\'s monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in this Section 9.1 and Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer\'s systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer\'s acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer\'s access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).

Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month, shall require at least seventy-two (72) hours\' advance written notice to Customer\'s designated technical contact, and shall be scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable. Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours\' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
**Section 9.2 --- Latency**

Vendor shall maintain API response latency at or below four hundred (400) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 400 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor\'s internal monitoring systems at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.
**Section 9.3 --- Model Accuracy**

Vendor shall maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score, at or above zero point ninety-four (F1 ≥ 0.94), as measured against the mutually agreed validation dataset established during the implementation process, following the conclusion of the Stabilization Period. The validation dataset and F1 score measurement methodology shall be documented in the applicable Statement of Work. The Parties shall review and, if necessary, update the validation dataset no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure it remains representative of Customer\'s production document processing workloads.

During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.90, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.

15: **[Section 1 --- Purpose and Scope]{.underline}**
16: 
17: This Playbook governs all procurement of artificial intelligence and machine-learning vendor services by TechNova Solutions, Inc. (\"TechNova\" or the \"Company\"). It establishes the mandatory negotiation positions, acceptable fallback concessions, and walk-away thresholds that must be followed by all personnel involved in the negotiation, drafting, review, and approval of AI/ML vendor agreements on behalf of TechNova.
18: 
19: This Playbook is jointly maintained by two departments within TechNova:
20: 
21: > • **Legal Department**, under the direction of the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions (currently Derek Chalmers); and
22: >
23: > • **Product Engineering**, under the direction of the VP of Product Engineering (currently Priya Anand).
24: 
25: These two departments share responsibility for the ongoing development, revision, and dissemination of the Playbook, and all substantive updates require joint sign-off from both maintaining teams prior to publication.
26: 
27: Every AI/ML vendor agreement entered into by TechNova must be negotiated consistent with the positions, fallbacks, and walk-away thresholds set forth herein. No TechNova employee, attorney, or agent is authorized to accept terms that fall below the minimum thresholds established in this Playbook without following the escalation and approval procedures described in Section 2. Compliance with this Playbook is mandatory and will be reviewed as part of the Company\'s internal contract compliance program.
28: 
29: The scope of this Playbook extends to all AI/ML platform agreements, software-as-a-service (SaaS) agreements for AI/ML-enabled tools, model-as-a-service engagements, and any related vendor engagements in which TechNova procures AI or machine-learning capabilities from a third-party vendor. This includes, without limitation, engagements involving large language models, natural language processing platforms, computer vision services, predictive analytics engines, recommendation systems, and any other AI/ML-enabled product or service. The Playbook applies regardless of the TechNova business unit initiating the procurement, and regardless of whether the engagement is structured as a master services agreement, a standalone statement of work, an order form, or any other contractual vehicle.
30: 
31: This is Version 3.2 of the Playbook, effective as of March 2025. Version 3.2 supersedes all prior versions of this Playbook, including Version 3.1 (September 2024), Version 3.0 (March 2024), and all earlier iterations. In the event of any conflict between this Playbook and a prior version, this Playbook controls. A complete version history is set forth in Section 13.

33: **[Section 2 --- Decision Matrix and Escalation Procedures]{.underline}**
34: 
35: **2.1 --- Classification Framework**
36: 
37: To ensure consistency and clarity in vendor negotiations, this Playbook classifies every material negotiation term according to a three-tier classification framework. Each tier corresponds to a defined level of concession authority and escalation requirement. The three tiers are as follows:
38: 
39: **Green (Preferred Position).** The Green tier represents TechNova\'s standard opening position on each negotiation term. This is the position that should be proposed in every initial draft of a vendor agreement. Acceptance of a Green-tier position by the vendor requires no escalation and no additional approval beyond the negotiating attorney\'s standard authority. The Green position represents TechNova\'s optimal outcome and should be pursued vigorously before any fallback is offered.
40: 
41: **Yellow (Acceptable Fallback).** The Yellow tier represents a concession that falls within an acceptable range below TechNova\'s preferred position. A Yellow-tier concession is one that in-house counsel at the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions level may approve without further escalation. The Yellow tier defines the outer boundary of what TechNova considers a commercially reasonable compromise on a given term. Negotiating attorneys should document the business rationale for accepting a Yellow-tier position in the negotiation file but are not required to seek approval from the VP Legal or General Counsel.
42: 
43: **Red (Walk-Away / Escalation Required).** The Red tier represents a concession that approaches or breaches TechNova\'s minimum acceptable threshold on a given term. A Red-tier position is one that the Company should ordinarily decline. If a negotiating attorney determines that acceptance of a Red-tier position may be warranted by extraordinary business circumstances, that acceptance requires written approval from the VP Legal prior to execution of the agreement. The VP Legal\'s approval must be documented in the deal approval memorandum and must include a written business justification and a description of the risk-mitigation measures that will be implemented.
44: 
45: The following additional rules apply to Red-zone concessions:
46: 
47: > • Any single Red-zone concession on any term in a vendor agreement requires written approval from the VP Legal prior to execution.
48: >
49: > • Two or more simultaneous Red-zone concessions on any single vendor agreement require joint approval from the VP Legal and the General Counsel. In such cases, the deal approval memorandum must include an enhanced risk assessment and a written recommendation from the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions.

77: **2.3 --- Escalation Procedures**
78: 
79: The escalation path for all AI/ML vendor negotiations follows the chain of authority set forth below:
80: 
81: 1\. **Negotiating Attorney** --- responsible for conducting the negotiation consistent with this Playbook, identifying the tier classification of each material term, and escalating as required.
82: 
83: 2\. **Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions** (currently Derek Chalmers) --- has authority to approve Yellow-zone concessions without further escalation. Serves as the first level of escalation for questions of interpretation under this Playbook.
84: 
85: 3\. **VP Legal** --- required approval authority for any single Red-zone concession. Serves as the second level of escalation.
86: 
87: 4\. **General Counsel** --- required co-approval authority (together with the VP Legal) for two or more simultaneous Red-zone concessions on any single vendor agreement. Serves as the final level of escalation.
88: 
89: Any acceptance of a Red-zone term must be documented in the deal approval memorandum. The memorandum must include, at minimum: (a) a description of the Red-zone concession and the vendor\'s stated rationale for its position; (b) a business justification for TechNova\'s acceptance of the concession; (c) a description of the risk-mitigation measures that will be implemented to address the risk associated with the concession; and (d) the written approval of the VP Legal (and, if applicable, the General Counsel).
90: 
91: Outside counsel may be engaged at the discretion of the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions for any AI/ML vendor engagement. Engagement of outside counsel is particularly recommended in the following circumstances:
92: 
93: > • Any engagement with a total contract value (\"TCV\") exceeding \$5,000,000.
94: >
95: > • Any engagement involving novel or untested AI/ML risk allocation issues, including but not limited to novel AI-output indemnity structures, regulatory compliance frameworks for generative AI, or cross-border data processing arrangements.
96: >
97: > • Any engagement where the vendor\'s proposed terms deviate materially from the positions established in this Playbook and the appropriate response is unclear.
98: 
99: TechNova\'s preferred outside counsel for AI/ML vendor transactions is Kirkstead & Yao LLP. Engagement of Kirkstead & Yao LLP or any other outside counsel must be authorized in writing by the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions and must comply with TechNova\'s outside counsel engagement policies.

101: **[Section 3 --- IP Ownership & Licensing]{.underline}**
102: 
103: **3.1 --- Preferred Position (Green)**
104: 
105: TechNova\'s standard opening position on intellectual property ownership and licensing is as follows:
106: 
107: **Ownership of Customer-Trained Adaptations.** TechNova owns all model artifacts that are derived from or trained on TechNova\'s data, including but not limited to: fine-tuned weights, adapter layers (including LoRA and QLoRA adapters), embeddings, vector representations, and any derivative models that incorporate TechNova data in any form (collectively, \"Customer-Trained Adaptations\"). This ownership extends to all rights, title, and interest in and to the Customer-Trained Adaptations, including all intellectual property rights therein, and such ownership vests automatically upon creation without the need for any further action or assignment.
108: 
109: **Vendor Retention of Base Model IP.** The vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing base model (the \"Base Model\") and all platform intellectual property that existed prior to the engagement or that is developed by the vendor independently of TechNova\'s data and without use of TechNova\'s confidential information. For the avoidance of doubt, the vendor\'s retained ownership does not extend to any Customer-Trained Adaptations, regardless of whether such adaptations are implemented on or integrated with the vendor\'s Base Model.
110: 
111: **License to Base Model.** TechNova receives an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free, fully sublicensable license to the vendor\'s Base Model solely as necessary to operate, deploy, maintain, and update the Customer-Trained Adaptations. This license survives expiration or termination of the agreement for any reason and includes the right to use the Base Model in production environments, disaster recovery environments, and development and testing environments as reasonably necessary for the operation of the Customer-Trained Adaptations.
112: 
113: This Green-tier position should be included in every initial draft of an AI/ML vendor agreement. It requires no escalation and no additional approval.
114: 
115: **3.2 --- Acceptable Fallback (Yellow)**
116: 
117: Where a vendor will not agree to assign ownership of Customer-Trained Adaptations to TechNova, TechNova will accept, as an alternative, an irrevocable, perpetual, worldwide, royalty-free license to all fine-tuned adapter weights and related Customer-Trained Adaptations, provided that all of the following conditions are met:
118: 
119: **Portability.** The vendor must provide an API-based or otherwise automated export of all Customer-Trained Adaptations in an industry-standard format (e.g., ONNX, SafeTensors, or other format mutually agreed upon at contract execution) within thirty (30) days of the termination or expiration of the agreement. The export must include all artifacts necessary for TechNova to deploy the Customer-Trained Adaptations on an alternative platform without material degradation in performance. The vendor may not condition the export on the payment of additional fees beyond those already payable under the agreement.
120: 
121: **Escrow.** All Customer-Trained Adaptations, together with training configuration files (including hyperparameters and training scripts) and pipeline artifacts necessary to reproduce or redeploy the fine-tuned model, must be deposited in escrow in accordance with the requirements set forth in Section 7 of this Playbook. The escrow deposit must be updated at least quarterly and upon any material model version update.
122: 
123: **Non-Assertion.** The vendor grants TechNova a perpetual, irrevocable covenant not to assert any intellectual property rights --- including patent, copyright, trade secret, and any other IP rights --- against TechNova\'s use, deployment, modification, or further development of Customer-Trained Adaptations, including post-termination use. This non-assertion covenant runs with any successor, assignee, or acquirer of the vendor\'s intellectual property rights.
124: 
125: This fallback position falls within the Yellow zone and may be approved by the Associate General Counsel -- Technology Transactions without further escalation, provided that all three conditions (portability, escrow, and non-assertion) are satisfied in full.
126: 
127: **3.3 --- Minimum Requirement / Walk-Away Threshold (Red)**
128: 
129: At absolute minimum, the agreement must grant TechNova a perpetual license to the Customer-Trained Adaptations that survives the termination or expiration of the agreement for any reason, together with extraction rights permitting TechNova to export all Customer-Trained Adaptations within thirty (30) days of termination or expiration.
130: 
131: Any vendor position that does not include at least a perpetual, surviving license with thirty-day extraction rights constitutes a walk-away and must not be accepted without written approval from the VP Legal. The VP Legal\'s approval must include a documented business justification explaining why the engagement is sufficiently critical to justify acceptance of a below-threshold IP position, together with a description of the alternative risk-mitigation measures (e.g., enhanced escrow, accelerated transition support) that will be implemented.
132: 
133: The following specific vendor positions fall within the Red zone:
134: 
135: > • A vendor position granting only a term-limited license that expires upon termination of the agreement, with no surviving rights to the Customer-Trained Adaptations.
136: >
137: > • A vendor position that conditions post-termination use of Customer-Trained Adaptations on the payment of additional license fees, maintenance fees, or any other fees not included in the original agreement pricing.
138: >
139: > • A vendor position that grants TechNova a surviving license but does not include extraction rights, or that conditions extraction on a timeframe longer than thirty (30) days.
140: 
141: **3.4 --- Negotiation Guidance**
142: 
143: Negotiating attorneys should adhere to the following approach when negotiating IP ownership and licensing terms with AI/ML vendors:
144: 
145: Open every negotiation with the full ownership position set forth in Section 3.1. Present TechNova\'s rationale clearly: the Customer-Trained Adaptations are derived from TechNova\'s proprietary data, and TechNova\'s investment in data curation, annotation, and preparation justifies ownership of the resulting artifacts. Many vendors will be receptive to this position, particularly where TechNova\'s data is the primary driver of the fine-tuning process.
146: 
147: If the vendor resists full ownership, move to the irrevocable perpetual license with portability, escrow, and non-assertion conditions set forth in Section 3.2. This concession does not require escalation and should be presented as a commercially reasonable compromise that protects both parties\' interests. Emphasize to the vendor that the non-assertion covenant and escrow requirements are essential counterbalances to TechNova\'s concession on ownership.
148: 
149: Under no circumstances should the negotiating attorney concede the thirty-day extraction window. The thirty-day period is a hard floor across all tiers of the classification framework. If a vendor proposes a longer extraction window (e.g., 60 or 90 days), this is not within the Yellow zone and must be treated as a Red-zone concession.
150: 
151: Finally, all IP ownership and licensing provisions must be reviewed for consistency with the escrow requirements in Section 7 and the indemnification scope in Section 11. The negotiating attorney should ensure that the escrow deposit scope in the agreement matches the defined scope of \"Customer-Trained Adaptations,\" and that the vendor\'s IP indemnification obligation extends to TechNova\'s authorized use of Customer-Trained Adaptations in addition to the vendor\'s Base Model and platform.
