**[ARTICLE 5 --- INTELLECTUAL PROPERTY]{.underline}**
**Section 5.1 --- Vendor IP Ownership**

As between the Parties, Vendor is and shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to: (a) the Platform; (b) the Base Model; (c) all Fine-Tuned Weights; (d) all Customer-Trained Adaptations; (e) all Derivative Models; and (f) all improvements, enhancements, updates, upgrades, modifications, and derivative works of any of the foregoing, together with all Intellectual Property Rights therein and thereto, regardless of whether such items are created by Vendor independently, in collaboration with Customer, or through the processing of Customer Data. For the avoidance of doubt, all fine-tuned weights, adapter layers, prompt-tuning parameters, and similar derivative model parameters generated through the fine-tuning, training, or adaptation of the Base Model using Customer Data shall be considered Derivative Models and are owned exclusively by Vendor. Customer hereby assigns, and agrees to assign, to Vendor all right, title, and interest that Customer may have or acquire in any Derivative Models, Customer-Trained Adaptations, or Fine-Tuned Weights, including all Intellectual Property Rights therein, and agrees to execute such documents and take such further actions as may be reasonably necessary to effectuate and perfect such assignment.
**Section 5.2 --- Customer Data Ownership**

As between the Parties, Customer is and shall remain the sole and exclusive owner of all right, title, and interest in and to all Customer Data, including all Intellectual Property Rights therein. Vendor\'s right to access, use, and process Customer Data is limited to the purposes expressly set forth in this Agreement, including providing the Platform, performing the Implementation Services, and the service improvement purposes described in Section 6.1. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed as transferring ownership of Customer Data from Customer to Vendor. Vendor acknowledges that Customer Data may contain NPPI and other regulated data, and Vendor agrees to treat all Customer Data in accordance with its obligations under this Agreement and applicable law.
**Section 5.3 --- Feedback**

If Customer or any of its employees, contractors, or agents provides any suggestions, enhancement requests, ideas, recommendations, corrections, or other feedback regarding the Platform, the Documentation, or any of Vendor\'s products or services (collectively, \"**Feedback**\"), Customer hereby grants to Vendor a worldwide, royalty-free, perpetual, irrevocable, fully paid-up, transferable, sublicensable license to use, reproduce, modify, adapt, create derivative works from, distribute, display, perform, and otherwise exploit such Feedback in any manner and for any purpose, without restriction, attribution, or compensation to Customer. Customer acknowledges that Vendor may use Feedback to improve the Platform, develop new features, or create new products or services, and that Vendor shall have no obligation to implement or incorporate any Feedback.
**Section 5.4 --- No Other Rights**

Except as expressly set forth in this Article 5 and the license granted in Section 2.1, neither Party grants the other Party any right, title, or interest in or to its Intellectual Property Rights, whether by implication, estoppel, or otherwise. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to grant Customer any rights in Vendor\'s trade secrets, proprietary algorithms, model architectures, training methodologies, or other confidential technical information, except as expressly provided herein.
**[ARTICLE 6 --- DATA PROCESSING AND PRIVACY]{.underline}**
**Section 6.1 --- Customer Data Processing**

Vendor shall process Customer Data solely for the following purposes: (a) providing the Platform and performing Vendor\'s obligations under this Agreement, including the Implementation Services; (b) operating, maintaining, supporting, and securing the Platform; and (c) service improvement purposes, including but not limited to improving the Base Model, developing new features and capabilities, training and validating Derivative Models, and conducting research and development related to Vendor\'s artificial intelligence products and services. For purposes of clause (c), Vendor may process Customer Data in de-identified and aggregated form such that the data does not identify or permit identification of Customer or any individual. Vendor shall implement appropriate technical measures to de-identify and aggregate Customer Data prior to its use for service improvement purposes. Vendor shall not sell Customer Data to any third party or use Customer Data for any purpose other than as expressly set forth in this Section 6.1.
**Section 6.2 --- Controller Status**

Each Party acknowledges that it acts as an independent data controller with respect to its own processing activities relating to Customer Data under this Agreement. Customer is the data controller with respect to Customer Data as it relates to Customer\'s internal business operations and its provision of Customer Data to Vendor. Vendor\'s processing of Customer Data for the purpose of providing the Platform under Section 6.1(a) and (b) shall be undertaken by Vendor on behalf of Customer. Vendor\'s processing of Customer Data for service improvement purposes under Section 6.1(c) shall be undertaken by Vendor as an independent data controller, and Vendor shall independently determine the purposes and means of such processing. Each Party shall be individually responsible for complying with its obligations under applicable data protection and privacy laws with respect to its processing activities as a data controller.
**Section 6.3 --- Compliance with Laws**

Each Party shall comply with all applicable data protection and privacy laws, rules, and regulations in connection with its processing of Customer Data under this Agreement, including without limitation: (a) the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 6801--6809, and its implementing regulations, including Regulation S-P (17 C.F.R. Part 248) and the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314) (\"**GLBA**\"), to the extent applicable to the processing of NPPI; (b) the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act of 2020, Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1798.100--1798.199.100 (\"**CCPA/CPRA**\"), to the extent applicable; and (c) any other applicable federal, state, or international data protection or privacy laws. To the extent required by applicable law, the Parties shall cooperate in good faith to enter into any additional data processing agreements or addenda necessary to comply with applicable data protection requirements.
**Section 6.4 --- Security Measures**

Vendor shall implement and maintain throughout the Term commercially reasonable administrative, technical, and physical safeguards designed to protect Customer Data against unauthorized access, acquisition, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction, consistent with industry standards for cloud-based enterprise software providers. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Vendor\'s security program shall include: (a) encryption of Customer Data in transit (using TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (using AES-256 or equivalent); (b) access controls, including multi-factor authentication, role-based access, and least-privilege principles; (c) regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing; (d) intrusion detection and prevention systems; (e) security incident response procedures; and (f) employee security awareness training. Vendor shall, upon Customer\'s reasonable request and no more than once per twelve (12)-month period, provide Customer with a summary of Vendor\'s then-current security measures and any SOC 2 Type II or equivalent audit reports covering Vendor\'s information security controls.
**Section 6.5 --- Data Breach Notification**

In the event of any confirmed security breach involving the unauthorized access, acquisition, use, or disclosure of Customer Data (a \"**Security Breach**\"), Vendor shall: (a) notify Customer of the Security Breach without unreasonable delay, and in any event within seventy-two (72) hours of confirmation of the Security Breach; (b) promptly investigate the Security Breach and take reasonable steps to contain, mitigate, and remediate the Security Breach; (c) provide Customer with reasonably detailed information regarding the nature and scope of the Security Breach, including the categories and approximate number of records affected, the likely consequences of the Security Breach, and the measures taken or proposed to address and mitigate the Security Breach; and (d) cooperate with Customer in Customer\'s investigation, response, and notification obligations in connection with the Security Breach. The obligations set forth in this Section 6.5 shall not be construed as an acknowledgment by Vendor of any fault or liability with respect to the Security Breach.
**Section 6.6 --- Return and Deletion of Data**

Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, Vendor shall, at Customer\'s written election made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration, either (a) return Customer Data to Customer in a commercially reasonable format designated by Customer, or (b) securely delete or destroy all Customer Data in Vendor\'s possession or control, including all copies, backups, and archives thereof. Vendor shall complete such return or deletion within sixty (60) calendar days of receipt of Customer\'s written request. Upon completion of the return or deletion, Vendor shall certify in writing to Customer that all Customer Data has been returned or deleted in accordance with this Section 6.6. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Vendor may retain copies of Customer Data to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, or legal hold obligation, provided that Vendor continues to protect such retained data in accordance with this Agreement. For the avoidance of doubt, data that has been de-identified and aggregated for service improvement purposes in accordance with Section 6.1 shall not constitute Customer Data for purposes of this Section 6.6 and shall not be subject to the return or deletion obligations set forth herein.
**[ARTICLE 7 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**
**Section 7.1 --- Definition of Confidential Information**

\"**Confidential Information**\" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of one Party (the \"**Disclosing Party**\") to the other Party (the \"**Receiving Party**\") in connection with this Agreement, whether disclosed orally, in writing, electronically, or by any other means, and whether or not marked or designated as \"confidential,\" \"proprietary,\" or with any similar legend, that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Confidential Information includes: (a) business plans, strategies, forecasts, and financial information; (b) technical information, including source code, algorithms, model architectures, model weights, training data, APIs, and system designs; (c) trade secrets; (d) customer lists, supplier lists, and pricing information; (e) product roadmaps and development plans; and (f) the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including all pricing, fee, and commercial terms. Customer Data shall be deemed Confidential Information of Customer regardless of whether it is marked or designated as confidential.

Confidential Information shall not include information that: (i) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of or breach by the Receiving Party; (ii) was already known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure by the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records; (iii) is rightfully received by the Receiving Party from a third party without restriction on disclosure and without breach of any obligation of confidentiality owed to the Disclosing Party; or (iv) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records.
**Section 7.2 --- Obligations**

The Receiving Party shall: (a) hold the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information in strict confidence; (b) not disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to any third party except as expressly permitted under Section 7.3; (c) use the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information solely for the purposes of performing its obligations or exercising its rights under this Agreement; and (d) protect the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information using commercially reasonable measures that are at least as protective as those used by the Receiving Party to protect its own confidential information of a similar nature, but in no event less than a reasonable standard of care.

The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article 7 shall remain in effect during the Term and for a period of five (5) years following the expiration or termination of this Agreement; provided, however, that the confidentiality obligations with respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under applicable law shall continue for so long as such information remains a trade secret.
**Section 7.3 --- Permitted Disclosures**

The Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to its employees, officers, directors, agents, contractors, consultants, advisors, and Affiliates who have a legitimate need to know such information for the purposes of this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article 7 (collectively, \"**Authorized Recipients**\"). The Receiving Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Article 7 by its Authorized Recipients.

The Receiving Party may also disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, court order, subpoena, or other legal process, provided that the Receiving Party: (a) provides the Disclosing Party with prompt written notice of such requirement (to the extent legally permitted) so that the Disclosing Party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy; (b) cooperates with the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party\'s expense, in seeking such protective order or other remedy; and (c) discloses only the minimum amount of Confidential Information necessary to comply with such requirement. Any Confidential Information disclosed pursuant to a legal compulsion shall retain its confidential status for all other purposes under this Agreement.
**[ARTICLE 8 --- REPRESENTATIONS AND WARRANTIES]{.underline}**
**Section 8.1 --- Mutual Representations and Warranties**
Each Party hereby represents and warrants to the other Party as of the date of this Agreement and as of the Effective Date that:
> \(a\) it is duly organized, validly existing, and in good standing under the laws of the jurisdiction of its formation;
> \(b\) it has full corporate or limited liability company power and authority to enter into this Agreement and to perform its obligations hereunder;
> \(c\) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement have been duly authorized by all necessary corporate or limited liability company action;

> \(d\) this Agreement constitutes a legal, valid, and binding obligation of such Party, enforceable against such Party in accordance with its terms, subject to applicable bankruptcy, insolvency, reorganization, moratorium, and similar laws affecting creditors\' rights generally and to general principles of equity; and

> \(e\) the execution, delivery, and performance of this Agreement will not (i) violate, conflict with, or result in a breach of any provision of such Party\'s organizational documents, (ii) violate any applicable law, rule, or regulation, or (iii) conflict with, result in a breach of, or constitute a default under any material agreement or instrument to which such Party is a party or by which it is bound.
**Section 8.2 --- Vendor Representations and Warranties**
Vendor hereby represents and warrants to Customer that:

> \(a\) the Platform, when used in accordance with the Documentation and this Agreement, will perform materially in accordance with the functional specifications set forth in the Documentation during the Term;

> \(b\) the Implementation Services will be performed in a professional and workmanlike manner, consistent with generally accepted industry standards for similar services, using personnel with the requisite skill, experience, and qualifications;

> \(c\) Vendor has all rights necessary to grant the license set forth in Section 2.1, free and clear of any liens, encumbrances, or restrictions that would materially impair Customer\'s exercise of the rights granted thereunder; and

> \(d\) to Vendor\'s knowledge as of the Effective Date, the Platform, as provided by Vendor and used in accordance with this Agreement, does not infringe any registered United States patent or registered United States copyright of any third party.

Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor\'s sole and exclusive liability, for any breach of the warranty set forth in Section 8.2(a) shall be for Vendor, at its option, to (i) repair or replace the non-conforming Platform functionality so that it conforms to the Documentation, or (ii) if Vendor is unable to repair or replace such functionality within a commercially reasonable period, terminate this Agreement and refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any prepaid Fees attributable to the period following such termination.
**Section 8.3 --- Disclaimer**

EXCEPT AS EXPRESSLY SET FORTH IN THIS ARTICLE 8, VENDOR MAKES NO WARRANTIES OF ANY KIND, WHETHER EXPRESS, IMPLIED, STATUTORY, OR OTHERWISE, WITH RESPECT TO THE PLATFORM, THE IMPLEMENTATION SERVICES, THE BASE MODEL, ANY DERIVATIVE MODELS, OR ANY OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM, INCLUDING WITHOUT LIMITATION ANY WARRANTIES OF MERCHANTABILITY, FITNESS FOR A PARTICULAR PURPOSE, NON-INFRINGEMENT, TITLE, ACCURACY, COMPLETENESS, RELIABILITY, OR QUALITY OF OUTPUTS. VENDOR DOES NOT WARRANT THAT THE PLATFORM WILL BE ERROR-FREE, UNINTERRUPTED, OR FREE OF HARMFUL COMPONENTS, OR THAT THE OUTPUTS GENERATED BY THE PLATFORM WILL BE ACCURATE, COMPLETE, OR SUITABLE FOR ANY PARTICULAR PURPOSE. CUSTOMER ACKNOWLEDGES THAT LARGE LANGUAGE MODELS ARE PROBABILISTIC IN NATURE AND THAT OUTPUTS MAY CONTAIN ERRORS, HALLUCINATIONS, OR INACCURACIES, AND CUSTOMER IS SOLELY RESPONSIBLE FOR EVALUATING AND VALIDATING ALL OUTPUTS FOR ITS INTENDED USE.
**[ARTICLE 9 --- SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SERVICE CREDITS]{.underline}**
**Section 9.1 --- Uptime**

Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain Platform availability of at least ninety-nine and nine-tenths percent (99.9%) in any calendar month (the \"**Uptime SLA**\"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:
> **Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100**

For purposes of the Uptime SLA, \"**Downtime**\" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor\'s monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer\'s systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer\'s acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer\'s access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).
**Section 9.2 --- Latency**

Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain API response latency at or below six hundred (600) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 600 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor\'s internal monitoring systems at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.
**Section 9.3 --- Model Accuracy**

Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score, at or above zero point ninety (F1 ≥ 0.90), as measured against the mutually agreed validation dataset established during the implementation process. The validation dataset and F1 score measurement methodology shall be documented in the applicable Statement of Work. The Parties shall review and, if necessary, update the validation dataset no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure it remains representative of Customer\'s production document processing workloads.
**Section 9.4 --- Service Credits**

In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA in any calendar month, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit B (each, a \"**Service Credit**\"). Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for the affected calendar month, as set forth in the tiered credit schedule in Exhibit B. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the Uptime SLA failure occurred.

Service Credits constitute Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor\'s sole and exclusive liability, for any failure to meet the service level commitments set forth in this Article 9. Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against Customer\'s next invoice(s) under this Agreement and shall not be refundable in cash. In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed twenty percent (20%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year.
**Section 9.5 --- Reporting**

Vendor shall provide Customer with monthly reports detailing Platform uptime, API latency, and model accuracy metrics for the preceding calendar month. Such reports shall be delivered to Customer within ten (10) business days following the end of each calendar month. Reports shall include, at a minimum: (a) Platform availability percentage; (b) total Downtime minutes and the cause of each incident; (c) API latency at the 50th percentile (p50) and 95th percentile (p95); (d) model accuracy metrics, including F1 score, precision, and recall, as measured against the validation dataset; and (e) API call usage data, including the total number of API calls consumed during the month and the cumulative total for the current Contract Year. Vendor shall make authorized Customer personnel available for a monthly service review meeting, upon Customer\'s reasonable request, to discuss the monthly reports and any performance issues.
**[ARTICLE 10 --- LIMITATION OF LIABILITY]{.underline}**
**Section 10.1 --- Exclusion of Consequential Damages**

IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, PUNITIVE, OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO DAMAGES FOR LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF REVENUE, LOSS OF GOODWILL, LOSS OF DATA, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES, COST OF PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES, BUSINESS INTERRUPTION, OR ANY OTHER COMMERCIAL DAMAGES OR LOSSES, WHETHER ARISING UNDER CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER LEGAL OR EQUITABLE THEORY, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES OR COULD HAVE FORESEEN SUCH DAMAGES. THE FOREGOING EXCLUSION SHALL APPLY REGARDLESS OF WHETHER SUCH DAMAGES ARISE FROM BREACH OF CONTRACT, BREACH OF WARRANTY, TORT, OR ANY OTHER CAUSE OF ACTION.
**Section 10.2 --- Aggregate Liability Cap**

EXCEPT AS SET FORTH IN SECTION 10.3, EACH PARTY\'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, WHETHER ARISING UNDER CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER LEGAL OR EQUITABLE THEORY, SHALL NOT EXCEED THE FEES ACTUALLY PAID OR PAYABLE BY CUSTOMER TO VENDOR DURING THE SIX (6)-MONTH PERIOD IMMEDIATELY PRECEDING THE DATE OF THE EVENT GIVING RISE TO THE CLAIM. FOR CLARITY, BASED ON THE ANNUAL PLATFORM FEE, THIS LIABILITY CAP EQUALS ONE MILLION TWO HUNDRED THOUSAND DOLLARS (\$1,200,000).
**Section 10.3 --- Exclusions from Cap**

The limitations and exclusions set forth in Sections 10.1 and 10.2 shall not apply to: (a) Customer\'s payment obligations under Article 4; (b) either Party\'s obligations under Article 7 (Confidentiality); (c) either Party\'s indemnification obligations under Article 11; (d) liability arising from a Party\'s gross negligence, willful misconduct, or fraud; or (e) liability arising from Vendor\'s breach of Section 6.4 (Security Measures) or Section 6.5 (Data Breach Notification) to the extent involving Vendor\'s gross negligence or willful misconduct.
**[ARTICLE 11 --- INDEMNIFICATION]{.underline}**
**Section 11.1 --- Vendor Indemnification**

Vendor shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Customer and its officers, directors, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"**Customer Indemnitees**\") from and against any third-party claim, suit, action, or proceeding alleging that Customer\'s authorized use of the Platform in accordance with this Agreement constitutes direct infringement of a registered United States patent or a registered United States copyright (each, an \"**IP Claim**\"), and shall pay all damages, costs, and expenses (including reasonable attorneys\' fees and court costs) finally awarded by a court of competent jurisdiction or agreed to in settlement of such IP Claim.

Vendor\'s obligations under this Section 11.1 are expressly limited to claims of direct infringement of registered United States patents and registered United States copyrights. Vendor shall have no indemnification obligation with respect to any claim based on or arising from:
> \(i\) trade secrets, trademarks, service marks, trade dress, or unregistered intellectual property rights of any kind;
> \(ii\) indirect infringement, contributory infringement, or inducement of infringement;

> \(iii\) Customer\'s combination of the Platform with any third-party products, services, hardware, software, data, or content not provided by Vendor, to the extent such combination gives rise to the infringement claim;
> \(iv\) Customer\'s modification, alteration, or customization of the Platform or its outputs, to the extent such modification gives rise to the infringement claim;
> \(v\) Customer\'s use of the Platform in violation of this Agreement, the Documentation, or applicable law;
> \(vi\) Customer\'s use of a version of the Platform other than the then-current version, if the infringement would have been avoided by use of the then-current version made available by Vendor; or
> \(vii\) any output generated by the Platform, to the extent the infringement claim relates to the content of such output rather than the Platform itself.
**Section 11.2 --- Vendor Remediation**
If the Platform becomes, or in Vendor\'s reasonable opinion is likely to become, the subject of an IP Claim, Vendor may, at its sole option and expense:
> \(a\) procure for Customer the right to continue using the Platform under terms substantially consistent with this Agreement;

> \(b\) modify or replace the Platform (or the infringing component thereof) to make it non-infringing, provided that such modification or replacement does not materially diminish the functionality of the Platform; or

> \(c\) if neither clause (a) nor clause (b) is commercially practicable in Vendor\'s reasonable determination, terminate this Agreement upon written notice to Customer and refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any prepaid Fees attributable to the period following such termination.

The remedies set forth in this Section 11.2, together with the indemnification obligations set forth in Section 11.1, shall constitute Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor\'s sole and exclusive liability, with respect to any IP Claim.

Customer shall defend, indemnify, and hold harmless Vendor and its members, managers, officers, employees, agents, successors, and assigns (collectively, the \"**Vendor Indemnitees**\") from and against any third-party claim, suit, action, or proceeding arising from or relating to:

lines.text: **[ARTICLE 9 --- SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SERVICE CREDITS]{.underline}**
**Section 9.1 --- Uptime**

Vendor shall maintain Platform availability of at least ninety-nine and ninety-five hundredths percent (99.95%) in any calendar month (the \"**Uptime SLA**\"). Platform availability shall be measured as follows:
> **Availability (%) = ((Total Minutes in Month − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes in Month) × 100**

For purposes of the Uptime SLA, \"**Downtime**\" means any period during which the Platform is unavailable to Customer for production use, as measured by Vendor\'s monitoring systems. The following events shall be excluded from the calculation of Downtime: (a) scheduled maintenance windows, subject to the limitations and notice requirements set forth in this Section 9.1 and Exhibit B; (b) Force Majeure Events as described in Section 14.5; (c) periods of unavailability caused by Customer\'s systems, networks, or equipment, or by Customer\'s acts or omissions; and (d) periods during which Customer\'s access is suspended by Vendor in accordance with this Agreement (including pursuant to Section 4.5).

Scheduled maintenance windows shall not exceed four (4) hours per calendar month, shall require at least seventy-two (72) hours\' advance written notice to Customer\'s designated technical contact, and shall be scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable. Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours\' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
**Section 9.2 --- Latency**

Vendor shall maintain API response latency at or below four hundred (400) milliseconds at the ninety-fifth percentile (p95 ≤ 400 ms) during each calendar month, as measured by Vendor\'s internal monitoring systems at the Platform\'s API gateway. Latency shall be measured as the time elapsed between Vendor\'s receipt of an API request at its API gateway and Vendor\'s transmission of the corresponding API response.
**Section 9.3 --- Model Accuracy**

Vendor shall maintain model accuracy, as measured by F1 score, at or above zero point ninety-four (F1 ≥ 0.94), as measured against the mutually agreed validation dataset established during the implementation process, following the conclusion of the Stabilization Period. The validation dataset and F1 score measurement methodology shall be documented in the applicable Statement of Work. The Parties shall review and, if necessary, update the validation dataset no less frequently than once per Contract Year to ensure it remains representative of Customer\'s production document processing workloads.

During the Stabilization Period (ninety (90) days following Go-Live), Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to achieve F1 ≥ 0.90, and shall work collaboratively with Customer to optimize model performance toward the post-stabilization target of F1 ≥ 0.94. Service Credits shall not accrue for model accuracy during the Stabilization Period.
**Section 9.4 --- Service Credits**

In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA, API Latency target, or Model Accuracy target in any applicable measurement period, Customer shall be entitled to a service credit in accordance with the service credit schedule set forth in Exhibit B (each, a \"**Service Credit**\"). Service Credits shall be calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for the affected calendar month, as set forth in the tiered credit schedule in Exhibit B. To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the SLA failure occurred.

Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against Customer\'s next invoice(s) under this Agreement . If this Agreement is terminated or expires and a balance of unapplied Service Credits remains, Vendor shall refund such balance in cash within thirty (30) days. In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed thirty percent (30%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year. Service Credits are not Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures. Customer retains all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity, including the termination right under Section 9.5.
\[ADDED: \### Section 9.5 --- Termination for Chronic SLA Failure

If Vendor fails to meet any SLA target (Uptime, Latency, or Accuracy) for three (3) or more consecutive calendar months, Customer shall have the right to terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days\' written notice, without payment of any early termination fee, and Vendor shall refund to Customer a pro-rata portion of any prepaid Annual Platform Fees for the period following the effective date of termination.\]
**Section 9.\[DELETED: 5\] \[ADDED: 6\] --- Reporting**

Vendor shall provide Customer with monthly reports in a machine-readable format detailing Platform uptime, API latency, and model accuracy metrics for the preceding calendar month. Such reports shall be delivered to Customer within five (5) business days following the end of each calendar month. Reports shall include, at a minimum: (a) Platform availability percentage; (b) total Downtime minutes and the cause of each incident; (c) API latency at the 50th percentile (p50) , 95th percentile (p95), and 99th percentile (p99); (d) model accuracy metrics, including F1 score, precision, and recall, as measured against the validation dataset; and (e) API call usage data, including the total number of API calls consumed during the month and the cumulative total for the current Contract Year. Customer shall have the right to independently verify reported metrics against its own monitoring data. Vendor shall make authorized Customer personnel available for a monthly service review meeting, upon Customer\'s reasonable request, to discuss the monthly reports and any performance issues.
**[ARTICLE 10 --- LIMITATION OF LIABILITY]{.underline}**
**Section 10.1 --- Exclusion of Consequential Damages**

IN NO EVENT SHALL EITHER PARTY BE LIABLE TO THE OTHER PARTY FOR ANY INDIRECT, INCIDENTAL, SPECIAL, CONSEQUENTIAL, PUNITIVE, OR EXEMPLARY DAMAGES, INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO DAMAGES FOR LOSS OF PROFITS, LOSS OF REVENUE, LOSS OF GOODWILL, LOSS OF DATA, LOSS OF BUSINESS OPPORTUNITIES, COST OF PROCUREMENT OF SUBSTITUTE GOODS OR SERVICES, BUSINESS INTERRUPTION, OR ANY OTHER COMMERCIAL DAMAGES OR LOSSES, WHETHER ARISING UNDER CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER LEGAL OR EQUITABLE THEORY, EVEN IF SUCH PARTY HAS BEEN ADVISED OF THE POSSIBILITY OF SUCH DAMAGES OR COULD HAVE FORESEEN SUCH DAMAGES. THE FOREGOING EXCLUSION SHALL NOT APPLY TO THE MATTERS DESCRIBED IN SECTION 10.3.
**Section 10.2 --- Aggregate Liability Cap**

EXCEPT AS SET FORTH IN SECTION 10.3, EACH PARTY\'S TOTAL AGGREGATE LIABILITY ARISING OUT OF OR RELATING TO THIS AGREEMENT, WHETHER ARISING UNDER CONTRACT, TORT (INCLUDING NEGLIGENCE), STRICT LIABILITY, OR ANY OTHER LEGAL OR EQUITABLE THEORY, SHALL NOT EXCEED TWO TIMES (2×) THE ANNUAL PLATFORM FEE, EQUAL TO FOUR MILLION EIGHT HUNDRED THOUSAND DOLLARS (\$4,800,000) (THE \"GENERAL CAP\").

**[ARTICLE 12 --- INSURANCE]{.underline}**

Notwithstanding the foregoing, Customer\'s consent shall be required for any assignment by Vendor to a direct competitor of Customer. Any purported assignment in violation of this Section 14.4 shall be null and void. Subject to the foregoing, this Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the Parties and their respective permitted successors and assigns.

Neither Party shall be liable for any delay or failure in the performance of any of its obligations under this Agreement (other than payment obligations) to the extent such delay or failure is caused by events or circumstances beyond such Party\'s reasonable control, including acts of God, natural disasters, earthquakes, floods, hurricanes, epidemics, pandemics, war, terrorism, riots, civil unrest, government actions or orders, embargoes, sanctions, labor disputes (other than those involving such Party\'s own employees), interruption or failure of telecommunications, internet, or power services, cyberattacks (to the extent not caused by such Party\'s failure to comply with its security obligations under this Agreement), or other causes beyond such Party\'s reasonable control (each, a \"**Force Majeure Event**\"). A Party\'s performance shall only be excused to the extent caused by the Force Majeure Event. The affected Party shall: (a) promptly notify the other Party of the Force Majeure Event and its expected duration; (b) use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate the impact of the Force Majeure Event and to resume performance as soon as practicable; and (c) keep the other Party reasonably informed of the status of the Force Majeure Event. No amendment, modification, or supplement to this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. No waiver of any provision of this Agreement, or of any right or remedy hereunder, shall be effective unless in a writing signed by the Party against whom the waiver is to be enforced. The Parties shall negotiate in good faith a valid, enforceable replacement provision that most closely reflects the original intent and economic effect of the invalid provision.

This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. **EXHIBIT A**
**STATEMENT OF WORK: IMPLEMENTATION AND FINE-TUNING SERVICES**
**(Initial SOW)**

This Statement of Work (\"**SOW**\") is entered into pursuant to Article 3 of the AI Platform Agreement dated as of April 2, 2025 (the \"**Agreement**\"), between Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC (\"**Vendor**\") and TechNova Solutions, Inc. (\"**Customer**\"). Capitalized terms used in this SOW but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Agreement. In the event of any conflict between this SOW and the Agreement, the terms of the Agreement shall control except as expressly stated herein.
**1. Scope of Implementation Services**
Vendor shall perform the following Implementation Services in connection with the deployment and configuration of the Platform for Customer\'s use with LendStream:

> **(a) Environment Provisioning.** Vendor shall provision and configure Customer\'s dedicated Platform environment, including allocation of compute resources, storage, and network infrastructure necessary to support Customer\'s anticipated workloads. Vendor shall configure Customer\'s environment with appropriate access controls, authentication mechanisms, and security settings in accordance with Vendor\'s standard security practices and Customer\'s reasonable security requirements.

> **(b) API Integration with LendStream.** Vendor shall provide technical assistance and support to Customer in integrating the Platform\'s APIs with Customer\'s LendStream product. Integration activities shall include API endpoint configuration, authentication and authorization setup, data format mapping, error handling design, and end-to-end connectivity testing. Customer shall be responsible for developing and maintaining all integration code on the LendStream side of the integration, with Vendor providing technical guidance and API documentation.

> **(c) Base Model Fine-Tuning on Customer Data.** Vendor shall fine-tune the Base Model using Customer Data to optimize the Platform\'s document processing, analysis, and classification capabilities for Customer\'s specific lending document types and workflows. Fine-tuning activities shall include data preprocessing, training dataset preparation, model training, hyperparameter optimization, and iterative testing and validation. Vendor shall conduct multiple training iterations as reasonably necessary to achieve the target model accuracy (F1 ≥ 0.90) against the mutually agreed validation dataset.

> **(d) Initial Accuracy Validation.** Vendor shall conduct accuracy validation testing of the fine-tuned model using the mutually agreed validation dataset. Vendor shall provide Customer with a detailed accuracy report, including F1 score, precision, recall, and per-category accuracy metrics. The Parties shall review the accuracy report and collaborate on any additional fine-tuning necessary to achieve the target accuracy metrics.

> **(e) Customer Personnel Training.** Vendor shall provide initial training to Customer\'s designated personnel on the use and operation of the Platform, including the API, user interfaces, dashboards, and reporting features. Training shall be delivered through a combination of live virtual instructor-led sessions and written training materials. Vendor shall provide up to sixteen (16) hours of live training, scheduled at mutually convenient times.
**2. Implementation Milestones and Payment Schedule**
**Milestone**     **Description**         **Target Date**            **Payment Trigger**
Milestone 1       Execution of this SOW   Upon Execution             \$425,000
Milestone 2       Go-Live                 October 1, 2025 (target)   \$425,000, subject to completion of acceptance testing under Section 3.5 of the Agreement
**Total Implementation Fee: \$850,000**

Invoices shall be issued within five (5) business days of achievement of each milestone and shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice, in accordance with Article 4 of the Agreement.
**3. Customer Responsibilities**
Customer shall be responsible for the following in connection with the Implementation Services:

> \(a\) **Data Delivery.** Customer shall deliver Customer Data to Vendor in the format and quality specifications reasonably specified by Vendor, in sufficient quantity and variety to support the fine-tuning and validation activities described in this SOW. Customer shall deliver the initial training dataset within fifteen (15) business days of execution of this SOW, and any additional data reasonably requested by Vendor within ten (10) business days of such request.

> \(b\) **Systems Access.** Customer shall provide Vendor with timely access to Customer\'s systems, environments, and networks as reasonably necessary for Vendor to perform the API integration and testing activities described in this SOW, including access to Customer\'s staging and testing environments for LendStream.

> \(c\) **Designated Points of Contact.** Customer shall designate qualified personnel to serve as the primary points of contact for the implementation project, including a business lead and a technical lead. Customer\'s designated business lead shall be **Priya Anand**, Senior Vice President, Lending Technology. Customer\'s designated technical lead shall be identified in writing within five (5) business days of execution of this SOW. Customer\'s designated contacts shall have the authority to make day-to-day decisions, provide approvals, and allocate Customer resources as necessary to support the implementation timeline.

> \(d\) **Timely Feedback and Approvals.** Customer shall provide feedback, approvals, and sign-offs at each milestone within five (5) business days of Vendor\'s request, unless a different timeline is mutually agreed.
**4. Vendor Responsibilities**
Vendor shall be responsible for the following in connection with the Implementation Services:

> \(a\) **Project Management.** Vendor shall assign a dedicated project manager to oversee the Implementation Services and serve as the primary point of contact for Customer. The project manager shall prepare and maintain a detailed project plan, facilitate regular status meetings (no less than weekly during active implementation), and provide written status reports to Customer on a bi-weekly basis.
> \(b\) **Technical Configuration.** Vendor shall perform all technical configuration, provisioning, and setup activities described in Section 1 of this SOW using qualified Vendor personnel.
> \(c\) **Fine-Tuning.** Vendor shall perform all model fine-tuning activities described in Section 1(c) of this SOW, using Vendor\'s standard fine-tuning methodologies and tools.

> \(d\) **Testing.** Vendor shall conduct comprehensive testing of the Platform environment, API integrations, and fine-tuned model prior to Go-Live, including functional testing, performance testing, and accuracy validation.
> \(e\) **Training.** Vendor shall develop and deliver the training program described in Section 1(e) of this SOW.
**5. Acceptance Criteria**
Acceptance of the Implementation Services shall be determined on a milestone-by-milestone basis as follows:
> \(a\) **Milestone 1 --- SOW Execution.** Milestone 1 shall be deemed achieved upon execution of this SOW by both Parties.

> \(b\) **Milestone 2 --- Go-Live.** Milestone 2 shall be deemed achieved upon mutual written sign-off by both Parties confirming that: (i) the Platform environment has been provisioned and configured; (ii) API integration with LendStream has been completed and tested; (iii) the fine-tuned model achieves a minimum F1 score of 0.90 against the mutually agreed validation dataset; and (iv) Customer personnel training has been completed. Go-Live is conditioned on the Platform performing materially in accordance with the Documentation.

If Customer identifies deficiencies in the deliverables for Milestone 2, Customer shall provide written notice to Vendor specifying the deficiencies in reasonable detail. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to remediate such deficiencies within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of Customer\'s notice. The Parties shall then repeat the acceptance review process. If the deficiencies are not remediated after two (2) additional remediation cycles, Customer may escalate the matter pursuant to the dispute resolution procedures in Section 14.2 of the Agreement.
**EXHIBIT B**
**SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SERVICE CREDIT SCHEDULE**

This Exhibit B is attached to and forms part of the AI Platform Agreement dated as of April 2, 2025 (the \"**Agreement**\"), between Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC (\"**Vendor**\") and TechNova Solutions, Inc. (\"**Customer**\"). Capitalized terms used in this Exhibit B but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Agreement. This Exhibit B sets forth the service level commitments applicable to the Platform and the service credit schedule applicable in the event of failure to meet such commitments, as referenced in Article 9 of the Agreement.
**1. Service Levels**
The following service level targets shall apply during the Term:
**Service Level**         **Target**                           **Measurement Period**                                  **Measurement Methodology**

**Platform Uptime**       ≥ 99.95%                             Calendar month                                          Vendor monitoring systems; calculated as ((Total Minutes − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes) × 100
**API Latency (p95)**     ≤ 400 ms                             Calendar month                                          Vendor API gateway metrics; 95th percentile response time
**Model Accuracy (F1)**   ≥ 0.94 (post-Stabilization Period)   Per validation dataset review (no less than annually)   F1 score measured against mutually agreed validation dataset

**Stabilization Period:** During the ninety (90)-day Stabilization Period following Go-Live, the Model Accuracy (F1) target shall be ≥ 0.90 (informational only; no Service Credits shall accrue for accuracy during the Stabilization Period).
**2. Scheduled Maintenance**

Vendor may schedule maintenance windows of up to four (4) hours per calendar month for the purpose of performing routine maintenance, upgrades, patches, and other operational activities on the Platform. Scheduled maintenance shall not be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA, provided that the following conditions are met:

> \(a\) Vendor provides Customer with at least seventy-two (72) hours\' prior written notice (via email to Customer\'s designated technical contact) of the scheduled maintenance window, specifying the date, start time, estimated duration, and nature of the maintenance activity;
> \(b\) Scheduled maintenance windows are scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 5:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable; and
> \(c\) The total duration of scheduled maintenance does not exceed four (4) hours in any single calendar month.

Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite seventy-two (72) hours\' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
**3. Force Majeure Exclusion**
Downtime resulting from Force Majeure Events, as defined in Section 14.5 of the Agreement, shall be excluded from the calculation of Platform availability for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
**4. Service Credit Schedule --- Uptime Failures**

In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA in any calendar month, Customer shall be entitled to a Service Credit calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment (\$200,000) for the affected calendar month, in accordance with the following tiered schedule:
**Monthly Uptime Achieved**         **Service Credit (% of Monthly Fee)**
\[ADDED: \### 4A. Service Credit Schedule --- Latency Failures

If p95 latency exceeds 400 ms for any calendar month, an additional Service Credit of 5% of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment (\$10,000) shall apply, subject to the overall monthly cap set forth in Section 5(c).\]
\[ADDED: \### 4B. Service Credit Schedule --- Accuracy Failures

If the F1 score falls below 0.94 for two (2) consecutive quarterly measurements (post-Stabilization Period), an additional Service Credit of 10% of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment (\$20,000) shall apply, subject to the overall monthly cap set forth in Section 5(c).\]
**5. Service Credit Terms and Conditions**

> \(a\) **Request Requirement.** To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor\'s support team within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the SLA failure occurred. The request must identify the specific dates and times of the SLA failure and reference the applicable monthly service report. Vendor shall validate the claim against its monitoring data and notify Customer of the approved Service Credit amount within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of the request.

> \(b\) **Application of Credits.** Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against the next invoice(s) issued to Customer under the Agreement. If this Agreement is terminated or expires and a balance of unapplied Service Credits remains, Vendor shall refund such balance in cash within thirty (30) days.

> \(c\) **Maximum Credits.** In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed thirty percent (30%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month (i.e., \$ 60,000). Service Credits are cumulative across SLA categories (Uptime, Latency, and Accuracy) but shall not exceed the thirty percent (30%) monthly cap in aggregate. Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year.

> \(d\) \*\* Remedies.\*\* Service Credits are not Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy for SLA failures. Customer retains all other rights and remedies available at law or in equity, including the termination right under Section 9.5 of the Agreement.
**6. \[DELETED: Latency and Accuracy\] \[ADDED: Termination Trigger\]**

If Vendor fails to meet any SLA target (Uptime, Latency, or Accuracy) for three (3) or more consecutive calendar months, Customer may terminate the Agreement upon thirty (30) days\' written notice in accordance with Section 9.5 of the Agreement, without payment of any early termination fee.

**ACCEPTABLE USE POLICY**

This Exhibit C is attached to and forms part of the AI Platform Agreement dated as of April 2, 2025 (the \"**Agreement**\"), between Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC (\"**Vendor**\") and TechNova Solutions, Inc. (\"**Customer**\"). This Acceptable Use Policy supplements the use restrictions set forth in Section 2.3 of the Agreement.
**1. Authorized Use**

Customer shall use the Platform solely for the processing, analysis, and classification of Customer Data in connection with Customer\'s LendStream product, as authorized under Section 2.2 of the Agreement.
**2. Prohibited Use**
Customer shall not use the Platform to process data of third parties other than Customer\'s end-user consumers in connection with LendStream.
**3. Legal Compliance**
Customer shall comply with all applicable laws in connection with its use of the Platform, including GLBA and CCPA/CPRA.
**4. Suspension for Violation**

Vendor may suspend Customer\'s access to the Platform for material violation of this Acceptable Use Policy, subject to prior written notice and a reasonable cure period of not less than ten (10) business days, except in cases of imminent security threat, in which case Vendor may suspend access immediately upon notice to Customer.\]

**EXHIBIT D**
**DATA PROCESSING ADDENDUM**

This Data Processing Addendum (\"**DPA**\") is attached to and forms part of the AI Platform Agreement dated as of April 2, 2025 (the \"**Agreement**\"), between Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC (\"**Vendor**\") and TechNova Solutions, Inc. (\"**Customer**\"). This DPA is entered into pursuant to Section 6.8 of the Agreement. In the event of any conflict between this DPA and the Agreement, this DPA shall control with respect to data protection matters.
**1. Scope.** This DPA applies to Vendor\'s processing of Customer Data as a service provider/processor on behalf of Customer.
**2. Role of the Parties**
Customer is the controller/business with respect to Customer Data. Vendor is the processor/service provider with respect to Customer Data and shall process Customer Data solely on behalf of Customer.
**3. CCPA/CPRA Service-Provider Certification**

Vendor certifies that it is a \"service provider\" as defined in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag), and that it shall not sell, share, or retain Customer Data except as necessary to perform its obligations under the Agreement.
**4. GLBA Compliance**
Vendor acknowledges that Customer Data includes consumer NPPI subject to the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act and agrees to comply with all applicable safeguard requirements thereunder.
**5. Processing Instructions**
Vendor shall process Customer Data solely in accordance with Customer\'s documented instructions as set forth in the Agreement.
**6. Sub-Processor Requirements**

Vendor shall not engage any sub-processor to process Customer Data without Customer\'s prior written consent. Vendor shall impose data protection obligations on sub-processors that are no less protective than those set forth in this DPA and the Agreement. Vendor shall remain fully liable for the acts and omissions of its sub-processors.
**7. Data Security**

Vendor shall implement and maintain SOC 2 Type II controls, encryption of Customer Data at rest and in transit, access controls, and logging and monitoring, as further described in Section 6.4 of the Agreement.
