lines.text: **12.4 Cooperation with Audits.** Vendor shall cooperate fully with all audits and inspections conducted under this Article, and shall provide Company and its authorized auditors with reasonable access to Vendor\'s relevant personnel, systems, facilities, documentation, and records. Vendor shall respond to all reasonable audit-related inquiries and requests for documentation within ten (10) business days of receipt, or such shorter period as may be reasonably necessary in the circumstances.

**12.5 Audit Costs.** Vendor shall bear its own internal costs of cooperating with audits conducted under this Article, including the costs of making personnel, systems, and documentation available to Company\'s auditors. Company shall bear the fees and expenses of its own auditors and external consultants. Notwithstanding the foregoing, if an audit reveals material non-compliance by Vendor with this DPA or Applicable Data Protection Laws, Vendor shall reimburse Company for the reasonable costs and expenses of the audit, including the fees and expenses of Company\'s external auditors.

**12.6 Remediation of Deficiencies.** Vendor shall promptly remediate any deficiencies, non-compliance, or security weaknesses identified during an audit conducted under this Article. Within fifteen (15) business days of receiving Company\'s written notice of audit findings, Vendor shall provide Company with a detailed written remediation plan, including the specific actions to be taken, the responsible parties, and the anticipated timeline for completion. Vendor shall implement the remediation plan within the agreed-upon timeline and shall provide Company with evidence of completion. Company reserves the right to conduct a follow-up audit to verify that the identified deficiencies have been remediated.

**12.7 Sub-Processor Audit Rights.** Company\'s audit rights under this Article extend to Sub-Processors engaged by Vendor to Process Personal Information on behalf of Company. Company may exercise such audit rights directly with respect to Sub-Processors, or may direct Vendor to conduct audits of its Sub-Processors on Company\'s behalf and provide Company with the results of such audits. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to include in its Sub-Processor agreements provisions granting Company (or Vendor, on Company\'s behalf) the right to audit the Sub-Processor\'s Processing activities related to Company\'s Personal Information.
**[Article 13 --- Cross-Border Transfer Mechanisms]{.underline}**

**13.1 Prohibition on Unauthorized Transfers.** Vendor shall not transfer, store, or Process Personal Information outside the United States without Company\'s prior written consent. For purposes of this Section, a \"transfer\" includes any access to Personal Information from a location outside the United States, whether by Vendor\'s personnel, Sub-Processors, or any third party acting on Vendor\'s behalf.

**13.2 Transfer Mechanisms.** Where cross-border transfers of Personal Information are authorized by Company in writing, Vendor shall ensure that appropriate transfer mechanisms are in place in compliance with Applicable Data Protection Laws prior to initiating any such transfer. Appropriate transfer mechanisms may include, as applicable: (a) the European Commission\'s Standard Contractual Clauses (SCCs); (b) binding corporate rules approved by a competent supervisory authority; (c) an adequacy decision by the relevant regulatory authority; (d) the EU-U.S. Data Privacy Framework, the UK Extension, or the Swiss-U.S. Data Privacy Framework; or (e) any other recognized transfer mechanism under Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor shall document the transfer mechanism relied upon for each cross-border transfer and make such documentation available to Company upon request.

**13.3 Transfer Impact Assessment.** Where required by Applicable Data Protection Laws or by Company, Vendor shall conduct and document a transfer impact assessment evaluating the laws and practices of the destination country to determine whether they provide an adequate level of protection for Personal Information. Vendor shall make the transfer impact assessment available to Company upon request and shall cooperate with Company in evaluating the adequacy of protections in the destination country.

**13.4 Supplementary Measures.** Vendor shall implement supplementary technical, organizational, and contractual measures as necessary to ensure an essentially equivalent level of protection for Personal Information transferred outside the United States. Such supplementary measures may include, without limitation: (a) additional encryption or pseudonymization measures; (b) enhanced access controls and monitoring; (c) contractual commitments from the data importer regarding government access requests; and (d) restrictions on onward transfers. Vendor shall consult with Company regarding the selection and implementation of supplementary measures.

**13.5 Notification of Changes Affecting Transfers.** Vendor shall promptly notify Company in writing of any changes in law, regulation, government practice, or other circumstances in the destination country that may materially affect the legality, adequacy, or enforceability of the cross-border transfer mechanism in place, or that may impair Vendor\'s ability to comply with its obligations under this Article. Upon receipt of such notification, the Parties shall consult in good faith to identify and implement alternative transfer mechanisms or supplementary measures. If no adequate alternative can be identified, Company shall have the right to suspend or terminate the affected cross-border transfer and, if necessary, terminate the Agreement or the affected services thereunder in accordance with Section 4.4.
**[Article 14 --- General Provisions]{.underline}**

**14.1 Order of Precedence.** In the event of any conflict, inconsistency, or ambiguity between the provisions of this DPA and the provisions of the Agreement (including any schedules, exhibits, or amendments thereto), this DPA shall control and take precedence with respect to the Processing of Personal Information. In the event of any conflict between the main body of this DPA and any exhibit or appendix hereto, the main body of this DPA shall control.

**14.2 Term.** This DPA shall become effective upon the date last signed by the Parties below (or, if executed concurrently with the Agreement, upon the effective date of the Agreement) and shall remain in effect for the duration of the Agreement. This DPA shall automatically terminate upon the termination or expiration of the Agreement, except that this DPA shall survive termination or expiration of the Agreement to the extent that Vendor retains any Personal Information in accordance with Section 11.4, and the obligations of confidentiality, data security, and data protection set forth herein shall continue to apply to any such retained Personal Information until such Personal Information is returned to Company or securely deleted and destroyed in accordance with Article 11.

**14.3 Amendments.** This DPA may not be amended, modified, supplemented, or waived except by a written instrument duly executed by authorized representatives of both Parties. No oral agreement, course of dealing, or course of performance shall be deemed to amend, modify, or supplement this DPA. Notwithstanding the foregoing, Company may update Exhibit C (Processing Description) from time to time by providing written notice to Vendor, and Vendor shall comply with such updates, provided that any update that materially increases the scope of Vendor\'s Processing obligations shall be subject to mutual agreement.

**14.4 Governing Law.** This DPA shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of \[**\_\_\_**\], without regard to its conflict of laws principles, consistent with the governing law provision of the Agreement. Any legal action or proceeding arising out of or relating to this DPA shall be brought in the courts specified in the dispute resolution provision of the Agreement.

**14.5 Liability.** The liability of each Party under this DPA shall be subject to the limitations and exclusions of liability set forth in the Agreement; *provided, however*, that the following shall not be subject to any limitation or cap on liability set forth in the Agreement: (a) Vendor\'s indemnification obligations arising out of a Data Breach caused by Vendor\'s failure to comply with its obligations under this DPA; (b) Vendor\'s liability arising out of willful misconduct, gross negligence, or fraud; (c) Vendor\'s liability arising from unauthorized Processing, sale, or sharing of Personal Information in violation of this DPA or Applicable Data Protection Laws; (d) Vendor\'s indemnification obligations for regulatory fines, penalties, or enforcement actions resulting from Vendor\'s breach of this DPA; and (e) any liability that cannot be limited or excluded under Applicable Data Protection Laws.

**14.6 Severability.** If any provision of this DPA is found by a court of competent jurisdiction to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable, such invalidity, illegality, or unenforceability shall not affect the remaining provisions of this DPA, which shall remain in full force and effect. The Parties shall negotiate in good faith to replace the invalid, illegal, or unenforceable provision with a valid provision that most closely approximates the intent and economic effect of the original provision.

**14.7 Entire Agreement.** This DPA, together with the Agreement (including all schedules, exhibits, and amendments thereto) and the exhibits attached hereto, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the Processing of Personal Information and supersedes all prior and contemporaneous negotiations, representations, warranties, commitments, offers, contracts, and writings relating to such subject matter, whether oral or written.

**14.8 Notices.** All notices, requests, demands, and other communications required or permitted under this DPA shall be in writing and shall be delivered in accordance with the notice provisions of the Agreement, with copies directed to:
> **Company Privacy Contact:**
> **Vendor Privacy Contact:**
Either Party may update its designated Privacy Contact by providing written notice to the other Party in accordance with this Section.

**14.9 Counterparts.** This DPA may be executed in two or more counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Facsimile and electronic signatures (including PDF, DocuSign, or similar electronic signature platforms) shall be deemed to be original signatures for all purposes.

**A.1 Purpose**

This Exhibit A describes the Technical and Organizational Measures (\"TOMs\") implemented and maintained by Vendor to protect Personal Information against unauthorized or unlawful Processing and against accidental loss, destruction, damage, alteration, or disclosure. These measures are referenced in Article 5 of the DPA and form an integral part thereof. Vendor shall implement and maintain these measures throughout the term of the DPA and shall update them as necessary to address evolving threats, vulnerabilities, and industry best practices.
**A.2 Organizational Security Measures**
Vendor shall implement and maintain the following organizational security measures:

> \(a\) **Information Security Governance.** Vendor shall maintain a formal information security governance structure, including a designated Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) or equivalent security officer with responsibility for the development, implementation, oversight, and enforcement of Vendor\'s information security program. The security officer shall report to Vendor\'s senior management on a regular basis regarding the status of the information security program.

> \(b\) **Security Awareness Training.** Vendor shall provide regular security awareness training to all personnel who have access to Personal Information, including employees, contractors, and temporary staff. Training shall be provided upon onboarding and at least annually thereafter, and shall cover topics including data handling procedures, phishing awareness, password security, incident reporting, and Vendor\'s obligations under this DPA and Applicable Data Protection Laws. Vendor shall maintain records of training completion.

> \(c\) **Background Checks.** Vendor shall conduct background checks on all personnel who will have access to Personal Information, to the extent permitted by Applicable Data Protection Laws and consistent with the sensitivity of the Personal Information to be accessed. Background checks shall be conducted prior to granting access and shall be appropriate to the role and level of access.

> \(d\) **Information Security Policies and Procedures.** Vendor shall maintain documented information security policies and procedures that address, at a minimum, data classification, access control, incident response, acceptable use, data retention and destruction, change management, and third-party risk management. Policies and procedures shall be reviewed and updated at least annually, and more frequently as needed to address changes in Vendor\'s operations, threats, or Applicable Data Protection Laws.
**A.3 Technical Security Measures**
Vendor shall implement and maintain the following technical security measures:

> \(a\) **Encryption Standards.** All Personal Information stored by Vendor shall be encrypted at rest using AES-256 encryption or an equivalent or stronger standard. All Personal Information transmitted by Vendor shall be encrypted in transit using TLS 1.2 or higher. Encryption key management practices shall follow industry best practices, including secure key generation, storage, rotation, and destruction.

> \(b\) **Access Control.** Vendor shall implement and maintain role-based access controls (RBAC) based on the principle of least privilege, ensuring that each user is granted only the minimum level of access necessary to perform their assigned duties. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) shall be required for all access to systems Processing Personal Information, including remote access and administrative access. Access rights shall be reviewed at least quarterly and promptly revoked upon personnel termination, role change, or when access is no longer required.

> \(c\) **Network Security.** Vendor shall implement and maintain firewalls, intrusion detection and prevention systems (IDS/IPS), and network segmentation to isolate systems Processing Personal Information from other systems and networks. Vendor shall monitor network traffic for anomalies and unauthorized activity on a continuous basis.

> \(d\) **Endpoint Protection.** Vendor shall deploy and maintain anti-malware software, endpoint detection and response (EDR) solutions, and host-based firewalls on all endpoints that access or Process Personal Information. Vendor shall ensure that all endpoint protection solutions are updated with current signatures and patches.

> \(e\) **Logging and Monitoring.** Vendor shall implement centralized log management and security event monitoring for all systems that Process Personal Information. Logs shall record, at a minimum, user authentication events, data access events, data modification events, data deletion events, and administrative actions. Logs shall be retained for a minimum of \[**\_\_\_**\] and shall be protected against unauthorized access, modification, or deletion. Vendor shall conduct regular review and analysis of logs to identify and respond to potential security incidents.

> \(f\) **Vulnerability Management.** Vendor shall conduct regular vulnerability scanning of its systems and infrastructure, no less frequently than quarterly, and shall conduct annual penetration testing by a qualified independent third party. Vendor shall implement a patch management program to ensure timely remediation of identified vulnerabilities, with critical and high-severity vulnerabilities remediated within the timeframes established by Vendor\'s vulnerability management policy (and in no event later than thirty (30) days of identification for critical vulnerabilities and sixty (60) days for high-severity vulnerabilities).

> \(g\) **Data Loss Prevention.** Vendor shall implement data loss prevention (DLP) measures to monitor, detect, and prevent unauthorized exfiltration or leakage of Personal Information, including DLP controls at the network, endpoint, and application layers.
**A.4 Physical Security Measures**
Vendor shall implement and maintain the following physical security measures:

> \(a\) **Physical Access Controls.** Vendor shall restrict physical access to data centers, server rooms, and other facilities where Personal Information is stored or Processed. Physical access shall be controlled through measures such as badge access systems, biometric authentication, security guards, and visitor escort policies.

> \(b\) **Environmental Controls.** Vendor\'s data centers and facilities shall be equipped with environmental controls, including fire detection and suppression systems, climate control (temperature and humidity monitoring), uninterruptible power supplies (UPS), backup power generators, and water damage detection systems.

> \(c\) **Visitor Access Policies.** Vendor shall maintain visitor access policies that require all visitors to data centers and facilities to sign in, present valid identification, be accompanied by authorized personnel at all times, and sign out upon departure. Visitor logs shall be maintained for a minimum of twelve (12) months.
**A.5 Business Continuity and Disaster Recovery**
Vendor shall implement and maintain the following business continuity and disaster recovery measures:

> \(a\) **Business Continuity Plan (BCP) and Disaster Recovery Plan (DRP).** Vendor shall maintain documented business continuity and disaster recovery plans that address the restoration of systems and data in the event of a disruption or disaster. BCPs and DRPs shall be tested at least annually through tabletop exercises, simulations, or live failover tests, and updated based on test results and changes to Vendor\'s operating environment.

> \(b\) **Backup Procedures.** Vendor shall maintain regular backup procedures for all Personal Information, with backups performed at a frequency appropriate to the criticality of the data. 414:

418:

421: **Section 13.3 --- Termination for Cause**
422: 
423: Either Party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice to the other Party if:
424: 
425: > \(a\) the other Party materially breaches any provision of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice from the non-breaching Party specifying the nature of the breach in reasonable detail; provided, however, that if the breach is not capable of cure within thirty (30) days, the breaching Party shall not be in default if it commences cure within such thirty (30)-day period and diligently pursues cure to completion within ninety (90) days after receipt of the initial notice; or
426: >
427: > \(b\) the other Party (i) becomes the subject of a voluntary or involuntary petition in bankruptcy or any proceeding relating to insolvency, receivership, liquidation, assignment for the benefit of creditors, or similar proceeding, and such petition or proceeding is not dismissed within sixty (60) days of filing, (ii) is dissolved or liquidated, or (iii) ceases to conduct business in the ordinary course.

430:

Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon one hundred eighty (180) days\' prior written notice to Vendor, subject to Customer\'s payment of an early termination fee equal to the remaining Annual Platform Fees that would have been due and payable through the end of the then-current term (i.e., the Initial Term or the then-current Renewal Term, as applicable), calculated as of the effective date of termination (the \"**Early Termination Fee**\"). The Early Termination Fee shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the effective date of termination. For the avoidance of doubt, the Early Termination Fee is intended to compensate Vendor for its lost revenue and is not a penalty.

433: **Section 13.5 --- Effects of Termination**
434: 
435: Upon the termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason:
436: 
437: > \(a\) all licenses granted to Customer under this Agreement, including the license granted in Section 2.1, shall immediately terminate, and Customer shall immediately cease all access to and use of the Platform;

439: > \(b\) Customer shall promptly destroy or return all copies of the Documentation and any other Vendor Confidential Information in Customer\'s possession or control, and shall certify in writing to Vendor that it has done so;

441: > \(c\) Vendor shall return or delete Customer Data in accordance with Section 6.6;
442: >
443: > \(d\) all Fees accrued and unpaid through the effective date of termination, together with any Early Termination Fee payable under Section 13.4, shall be immediately due and payable; and
444: >
445: > \(e\) each Party shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information of the other Party in its possession or control, subject to the exceptions set forth in Section 6.6 and Section 7.2.

447: **Survival.** The following provisions shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason: Article 1 (Definitions), Article 5 (Intellectual Property), Article 7 (Confidentiality), Article 10 (Limitation of Liability), Article 11 (Indemnification), and Article 14 (General Provisions), as well as Sections 4.4 (Taxes), 4.5 (Late Payments), 6.6 (Return and Deletion of Data), 8.3 (Disclaimer), and this Section 13.5. In addition, any provision of this Agreement that by its nature or context is intended to survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement shall so survive.

452: 
453: This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, without regard to its conflict of laws principles that would require or permit the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods shall not apply to this Agreement.

456: 
457: Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or validity thereof, shall be resolved by binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association (\"**AAA**\") in accordance with its Commercial Arbitration Rules then in effect. The arbitration shall be conducted in Boston, Massachusetts by a panel of three (3) arbitrators selected in accordance with the AAA\'s procedures. The arbitrators shall have expertise in technology transactions. The language of the arbitration shall be English.

545: This Statement of Work (\"**SOW**\") is entered into pursuant to Article 3 of the AI Platform Agreement dated as of April 2, 2025 (the \"**Agreement**\"), between Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC (\"**Vendor**\") and TechNova Solutions, Inc. 547: **1. Scope of Implementation Services**
548: 
549: Vendor shall perform the following Implementation Services in connection with the deployment and configuration of the Platform for Customer\'s use with LendStream:
550: 
551: > **(a) Environment Provisioning.** Vendor shall provision and configure Customer\'s dedicated Platform environment, including allocation of compute resources, storage, and network infrastructure necessary to support Customer\'s anticipated workloads. Vendor shall configure Customer\'s environment with appropriate access controls, authentication mechanisms, and security settings in accordance with Vendor\'s standard security practices and Customer\'s reasonable security requirements.
552: >
553: > **(b) API Integration with LendStream.** Vendor shall provide technical assistance and support to Customer in integrating the Platform\'s APIs with Customer\'s LendStream product. Integration activities shall include API endpoint configuration, authentication and authorization setup, data format mapping, error handling design, and end-to-end connectivity testing. Customer shall be responsible for developing and maintaining all integration code on the LendStream side of the integration, with Vendor providing technical guidance and API documentation.
554: >
555: > **(c) Base Model Fine-Tuning on Customer Data.** Vendor shall fine-tune the Base Model using Customer Data to optimize the Platform\'s document processing, analysis, and classification capabilities for Customer\'s specific lending document types and workflows. Fine-tuning activities shall include data preprocessing, training dataset preparation, model training, hyperparameter optimization, and iterative testing and validation. Vendor shall conduct multiple training iterations as reasonably necessary to achieve the target model accuracy (F1 ≥ 0.90) against the mutually agreed validation dataset.
556: >
557: > **(d) Initial Accuracy Validation.** Vendor shall conduct accuracy validation testing of the fine-tuned model using the mutually agreed validation dataset. Vendor shall provide Customer with a detailed accuracy report, including F1 score, precision, recall, and per-category accuracy metrics. The Parties shall review the accuracy report and collaborate on any additional fine-tuning necessary to achieve the target accuracy metrics.
558: >
559: > **(e) Customer Personnel Training.** Vendor shall provide initial training to Customer\'s designated personnel on the use and operation of the Platform, including the API, user interfaces, dashboards, and reporting features. Training shall be delivered through a combination of live virtual instructor-led sessions and written training materials. Vendor shall provide up to sixteen (16) hours of live training, scheduled at mutually convenient times.

581: > \(b\) **Systems Access.** Customer shall provide Vendor with timely access to Customer\'s systems, environments, and networks as reasonably necessary for Vendor to perform the API integration and testing activities described in this SOW, including access to Customer\'s staging and testing environments for LendStream.

Customer\'s designated technical lead shall be identified in writing within five (5) business days of execution of this SOW. The project manager shall prepare and maintain a detailed project plan, facilitate regular status meetings (no less than weekly during active implementation), and provide written status reports to Customer on a bi-weekly basis.
592: >
593: > \(b\) **Technical Configuration.** Vendor shall perform all technical configuration, provisioning, and setup activities described in Section 1 of this SOW using qualified Vendor personnel.
594: >
595: > \(c\) **Fine-Tuning.** Vendor shall perform all model fine-tuning activities described in Section 1(c) of this SOW, using Vendor\'s standard fine-tuning methodologies and tools.
596: >
597: > \(d\) **Testing.** Vendor shall conduct comprehensive testing of the Platform environment, API integrations, and fine-tuned model prior to Go-Live, including functional testing, performance testing, and accuracy validation.
598: >
599: > \(e\) **Training.** Vendor shall develop and deliver the training program described in Section 1(e) of this SOW.

603: Acceptance of the Implementation Services shall be determined on a milestone-by-milestone basis as follows:
604: 
605: > \(a\) **Milestone 1 --- SOW Execution.** Milestone 1 shall be deemed achieved upon execution of this SOW by both Parties.
606: >
607: > \(b\) **Milestone 2 --- Go-Live.** Milestone 2 shall be deemed achieved upon mutual written sign-off by both Parties confirming that: (i) the Platform environment has been provisioned and configured; (ii) API integration with LendStream has been completed and tested; (iii) the fine-tuned model achieves a minimum F1 score of 0.90 against the mutually agreed validation dataset; and (iv) Customer personnel training has been completed. Go-Live is conditioned on the Platform performing materially in accordance with the Documentation.

**[ARTICLE 12 --- INSURANCE]{.underline}**
**Section 12.1 --- Vendor Insurance Requirements**

Vendor shall obtain and maintain in full force and effect during the Term and for a period of two (2) years following the expiration or termination of this Agreement the following minimum insurance coverages, with insurance carriers rated A- VII or better by A.M. Best:

> \(a\) **Commercial General Liability Insurance:** Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) per occurrence and Ten Million Dollars (\$10,000,000) in the annual aggregate, covering bodily injury, property damage, personal injury, and advertising injury, including contractual liability coverage;

> \(b\) **Technology Errors & Omissions / Cyber Liability Insurance:** Five Million Dollars (\$5,000,000) per occurrence, covering claims arising from errors, omissions, or negligent acts in the performance of technology services, as well as data breaches, unauthorized access, network security failures, and privacy liability;

> \(d\) **Workers\' Compensation Insurance:** as required by applicable law, with statutory limits, and Employers\' Liability Insurance with limits of not less than One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) per accident, One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) per employee for disease, and One Million Dollars (\$1,000,000) policy limit for disease; and

Vendor shall provide Customer with certificates of insurance evidencing the coverages required under Section 12.1 within ten (10) business days of the Effective Date and upon each annual renewal thereafter, or at any time upon Customer\'s reasonable written request. **Section 13.1 --- Initial Term**

**Section 13.2 --- Renewal**

Following the expiration of the Initial Term, this Agreement shall automatically renew for successive twelve (12)-month periods (each, a \"**Renewal Term**\"), unless either Party provides written notice of non-renewal to the other Party at least one hundred eighty (180) days prior to the expiration of the then-current term (i.e., the Initial Term or any Renewal Term, as applicable). All other terms and conditions of this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect during each Renewal Term.
**Section 13.3 --- Termination for Cause**
Either Party may terminate this Agreement upon written notice to the other Party if:

> \(a\) the other Party materially breaches any provision of this Agreement and fails to cure such breach within thirty (30) days after receipt of written notice from the non-breaching Party specifying the nature of the breach in reasonable detail; provided, however, that if the breach is not capable of cure within thirty (30) days, the breaching Party shall not be in default if it commences cure within such thirty (30)-day period and diligently pursues cure to completion within ninety (90) days after receipt of the initial notice; or

> \(b\) the other Party (i) becomes the subject of a voluntary or involuntary petition in bankruptcy or any proceeding relating to insolvency, receivership, liquidation, assignment for the benefit of creditors, or similar proceeding, and such petition or proceeding is not dismissed within sixty (60) days of filing, (ii) is dissolved or liquidated, or (iii) ceases to conduct business in the ordinary course.
**Section 13.4 --- Termination for Convenience**

Vendor shall not have the right to terminate this Agreement for convenience. Customer may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon one hundred eighty (180) days\' prior written notice to Vendor, subject to Customer\'s payment of an early termination fee equal to the remaining Annual Platform Fees that would have been due and payable through the end of the then-current term (i.e., the Initial Term or the then-current Renewal Term, as applicable), calculated as of the effective date of termination (the \"**Early Termination Fee**\"). The Early Termination Fee shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the effective date of termination. For the avoidance of doubt, the Early Termination Fee is intended to compensate Vendor for its lost revenue and is not a penalty.
**Section 13.5 --- Effects of Termination**
Upon the termination or expiration of this Agreement for any reason:

> \(a\) all licenses granted to Customer under this Agreement, including the license granted in Section 2.1, shall immediately terminate, and Customer shall immediately cease all access to and use of the Platform;

> \(b\) Customer shall promptly destroy or return all copies of the Documentation and any other Vendor Confidential Information in Customer\'s possession or control, and shall certify in writing to Vendor that it has done so;
> \(c\) Vendor shall return or delete Customer Data in accordance with Section 6.6;
> \(d\) all Fees accrued and unpaid through the effective date of termination, together with any Early Termination Fee payable under Section 13.4, shall be immediately due and payable; and
> \(e\) each Party shall promptly return or destroy all Confidential Information of the other Party in its possession or control, subject to the exceptions set forth in Section 6.6 and Section 7.2.

**Survival.** The following provisions shall survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement for any reason: Article 1 (Definitions), Article 5 (Intellectual Property), Article 7 (Confidentiality), Article 10 (Limitation of Liability), Article 11 (Indemnification), and Article 14 (General Provisions), as well as Sections 4.4 (Taxes), 4.5 (Late Payments), 6.6 (Return and Deletion of Data), 8.3 (Disclaimer), and this Section 13.5. In addition, any provision of this Agreement that by its nature or context is intended to survive the expiration or termination of this Agreement shall so survive.
**[ARTICLE 14 --- GENERAL PROVISIONS]{.underline}**
**Section 14.1 --- Governing Law**

This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the Commonwealth of Massachusetts, without regard to its conflict of laws principles that would require or permit the application of the laws of any other jurisdiction. The United Nations Convention on Contracts for the International Sale of Goods shall not apply to this Agreement.
**Section 14.2 --- Dispute Resolution**

Any dispute, controversy, or claim arising out of or relating to this Agreement, or the breach, termination, or validity thereof, shall be resolved by binding arbitration administered by the American Arbitration Association (\"**AAA**\") in accordance with its Commercial Arbitration Rules then in effect. The arbitration shall be conducted in Boston, Massachusetts by a panel of three (3) arbitrators selected in accordance with the AAA\'s procedures. The arbitrators shall have expertise in technology transactions. The language of the arbitration shall be English.

The decision of the arbitrators shall be final and binding upon the Parties and may be entered as a judgment in any court of competent jurisdiction. The arbitrators shall have the authority to award any remedy or relief that a court of competent jurisdiction could award, including injunctive relief, specific performance, and damages, but shall not have the authority to award punitive or exemplary damages.

Each Party shall bear its own costs and attorneys\' fees in connection with the arbitration, unless the arbitrators determine that the circumstances warrant an award of costs and fees to the prevailing Party. The costs of the arbitration, including the arbitrators\' fees and expenses, shall be borne equally by the Parties, unless the arbitrators determine otherwise.

Notwithstanding the foregoing, either Party may seek temporary or preliminary injunctive relief from any court of competent jurisdiction to prevent irreparable harm pending the outcome of arbitration, without the necessity of posting a bond or other security.
**Section 14.3 --- Notices**

All notices, demands, requests, consents, approvals, and other communications (collectively, \"**Notices**\") required or permitted under this Agreement shall be in writing and shall be deemed duly given and effective: (a) upon delivery, if delivered by hand during normal business hours; (b) one (1) business day after deposit with a nationally recognized overnight courier service, with delivery charges prepaid; or (c) three (3) business days after deposit in the United States mail, certified or registered, return receipt requested, postage prepaid, in each case addressed to the applicable Party at the following address (or such other address as a Party may designate by Notice given in accordance with this Section 14.3):

Any purported assignment in violation of this Section 14.4 shall be null and void. Subject to the foregoing, this Agreement shall be binding upon and inure to the benefit of the Parties and their respective permitted successors and assigns.
**Section 14.5 --- Force Majeure**

Neither Party shall be liable for any delay or failure in the performance of any of its obligations under this Agreement (other than payment obligations) to the extent such delay or failure is caused by events or circumstances beyond such Party\'s reasonable control, including acts of God, natural disasters, earthquakes, floods, hurricanes, epidemics, pandemics, war, terrorism, riots, civil unrest, government actions or orders, embargoes, sanctions, labor disputes (other than those involving such Party\'s own employees), interruption or failure of telecommunications, internet, or power services, cyberattacks (to the extent not caused by such Party\'s failure to comply with its security obligations under this Agreement), or other causes beyond such Party\'s reasonable control (each, a \"**Force Majeure Event**\"). The affected Party shall: (a) promptly notify the other Party of the Force Majeure Event and its expected duration; (b) use commercially reasonable efforts to mitigate the impact of the Force Majeure Event and to resume performance as soon as practicable; and (c) keep the other Party reasonably informed of the status of the Force Majeure Event. If a Force Majeure Event continues for more than ninety (90) consecutive days, either Party may terminate this Agreement upon thirty (30) days\' written notice to the other Party.
**Section 14.6 --- Entire Agreement**

This Agreement, together with all Exhibits, Schedules, and Statements of Work attached hereto or incorporated by reference herein, constitutes the entire agreement between the Parties with respect to the subject matter hereof and supersedes all prior or contemporaneous agreements, proposals, negotiations, representations, warranties, understandings, and communications between the Parties, whether written or oral, relating to such subject matter. No amendment, modification, or supplement to this Agreement shall be effective unless in writing and signed by authorized representatives of both Parties. No waiver of any provision of this Agreement, or of any right or remedy hereunder, shall be effective unless in a writing signed by the Party against whom the waiver is to be enforced. No waiver of any provision shall be deemed a waiver of any other provision, nor shall any single or partial exercise of any right or remedy preclude any further exercise of the same or any other right or remedy.
**Section 14.8 --- Severability**

If any provision of this Agreement is held to be invalid, illegal, or unenforceable by a court of competent jurisdiction or arbitral tribunal, the validity, legality, and enforceability of the remaining provisions shall not in any way be affected or impaired thereby. The Parties shall negotiate in good faith a valid, enforceable replacement provision that most closely reflects the original intent and economic effect of the invalid provision.
**Section 14.9 --- Counterparts**

This Agreement may be executed in any number of counterparts, each of which shall be deemed an original, and all of which together shall constitute one and the same instrument. Execution and delivery of this Agreement by electronic means, including by electronic signature (e.g., DocuSign or similar platform) or by the exchange of PDF copies bearing the Parties\' signatures, shall be deemed effective as delivery of a manually executed original for all purposes.
**Section 14.10 --- Independent Contractor**

The relationship between Vendor and Customer established by this Agreement is that of independent contractors. Nothing in this Agreement shall be construed to create a partnership, joint venture, employment relationship, or agency relationship between the Parties. **STATEMENT OF WORK: IMPLEMENTATION AND FINE-TUNING SERVICES**
**(Initial SOW)**

This Statement of Work (\"**SOW**\") is entered into pursuant to Article 3 of the AI Platform Agreement dated as of April 2, 2025 (the \"**Agreement**\"), between Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC (\"**Vendor**\") and TechNova Solutions, Inc. (\"**Customer**\"). Capitalized terms used in this SOW but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Agreement. In the event of any conflict between this SOW and the Agreement, the terms of the Agreement shall control except as expressly stated herein.
**1. Scope of Implementation Services**
Vendor shall perform the following Implementation Services in connection with the deployment and configuration of the Platform for Customer\'s use with LendStream:

> **(a) Environment Provisioning.** Vendor shall provision and configure Customer\'s dedicated Platform environment, including allocation of compute resources, storage, and network infrastructure necessary to support Customer\'s anticipated workloads. Vendor shall configure Customer\'s environment with appropriate access controls, authentication mechanisms, and security settings in accordance with Vendor\'s standard security practices and Customer\'s reasonable security requirements.

> **(b) API Integration with LendStream.** Vendor shall provide technical assistance and support to Customer in integrating the Platform\'s APIs with Customer\'s LendStream product. Integration activities shall include API endpoint configuration, authentication and authorization setup, data format mapping, error handling design, and end-to-end connectivity testing. Customer shall be responsible for developing and maintaining all integration code on the LendStream side of the integration, with Vendor providing technical guidance and API documentation.

> **(c) Base Model Fine-Tuning on Customer Data.** Vendor shall fine-tune the Base Model using Customer Data to optimize the Platform\'s document processing, analysis, and classification capabilities for Customer\'s specific lending document types and workflows. Fine-tuning activities shall include data preprocessing, training dataset preparation, model training, hyperparameter optimization, and iterative testing and validation. Vendor shall conduct multiple training iterations as reasonably necessary to achieve the target model accuracy (F1 ≥ 0.90) against the mutually agreed validation dataset.

> **(d) Initial Accuracy Validation.** Vendor shall conduct accuracy validation testing of the fine-tuned model using the mutually agreed validation dataset. Vendor shall provide Customer with a detailed accuracy report, including F1 score, precision, recall, and per-category accuracy metrics. The Parties shall review the accuracy report and collaborate on any additional fine-tuning necessary to achieve the target accuracy metrics.

> **(e) Customer Personnel Training.** Vendor shall provide initial training to Customer\'s designated personnel on the use and operation of the Platform, including the API, user interfaces, dashboards, and reporting features. Training shall be delivered through a combination of live virtual instructor-led sessions and written training materials. Vendor shall provide up to sixteen (16) hours of live training, scheduled at mutually convenient times.
**2. Implementation Milestones and Payment Schedule**
**Milestone**     **Description**         **Target Date**            **Payment Trigger**
Milestone 1       Execution of this SOW   Upon Execution             \$425,000
Milestone 2       Go-Live                 October 1, 2025 (target)   \$425,000
**Total Implementation Fee: \$850,000**

Invoices shall be issued within five (5) business days of achievement of each milestone and shall be due and payable within thirty (30) days of the date of invoice, in accordance with Article 4 of the Agreement.
**3. Customer Responsibilities**
Customer shall be responsible for the following in connection with the Implementation Services:

> \(a\) **Data Delivery.** Customer shall deliver Customer Data to Vendor in the format and quality specifications reasonably specified by Vendor, in sufficient quantity and variety to support the fine-tuning and validation activities described in this SOW. Customer shall deliver the initial training dataset within fifteen (15) business days of execution of this SOW, and any additional data reasonably requested by Vendor within ten (10) business days of such request.

> \(b\) **Systems Access.** Customer shall provide Vendor with timely access to Customer\'s systems, environments, and networks as reasonably necessary for Vendor to perform the API integration and testing activities described in this SOW, including access to Customer\'s staging and testing environments for LendStream.

> \(c\) **Designated Points of Contact.** Customer shall designate qualified personnel to serve as the primary points of contact for the implementation project, including a business lead and a technical lead. Customer\'s designated business lead shall be **Priya Anand**, Senior Vice President, Lending Technology. Customer\'s designated technical lead shall be identified in writing within five (5) business days of execution of this SOW. Customer\'s designated contacts shall have the authority to make day-to-day decisions, provide approvals, and allocate Customer resources as necessary to support the implementation timeline.

> \(d\) **Timely Feedback and Approvals.** Customer shall provide feedback, approvals, and sign-offs at each milestone within five (5) business days of Vendor\'s request, unless a different timeline is mutually agreed.
**4. Vendor Responsibilities**
Vendor shall be responsible for the following in connection with the Implementation Services:

> \(a\) **Project Management.** Vendor shall assign a dedicated project manager to oversee the Implementation Services and serve as the primary point of contact for Customer. The project manager shall prepare and maintain a detailed project plan, facilitate regular status meetings (no less than weekly during active implementation), and provide written status reports to Customer on a bi-weekly basis.
> \(b\) **Technical Configuration.** Vendor shall perform all technical configuration, provisioning, and setup activities described in Section 1 of this SOW using qualified Vendor personnel.
> \(c\) **Fine-Tuning.** Vendor shall perform all model fine-tuning activities described in Section 1(c) of this SOW, using Vendor\'s standard fine-tuning methodologies and tools.

> \(d\) **Testing.** Vendor shall conduct comprehensive testing of the Platform environment, API integrations, and fine-tuned model prior to Go-Live, including functional testing, performance testing, and accuracy validation.
> \(e\) **Training.** Vendor shall develop and deliver the training program described in Section 1(e) of this SOW.
**5. Acceptance Criteria**
Acceptance of the Implementation Services shall be determined on a milestone-by-milestone basis as follows:
> \(a\) **Milestone 1 --- SOW Execution.** Milestone 1 shall be deemed achieved upon execution of this SOW by both Parties.

> \(b\) **Milestone 2 --- Go-Live.** Milestone 2 shall be deemed achieved upon mutual written sign-off by both Parties confirming that: (i) the Platform environment has been provisioned and configured; (ii) API integration with LendStream has been completed and tested; (iii) the fine-tuned model achieves a minimum F1 score of 0.90 against the mutually agreed validation dataset; and (iv) Customer personnel training has been completed. Go-Live is conditioned on the Platform performing materially in accordance with the Documentation.

If Customer identifies deficiencies in the deliverables for Milestone 2, Customer shall provide written notice to Vendor specifying the deficiencies in reasonable detail. Vendor shall use commercially reasonable efforts to remediate such deficiencies within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of Customer\'s notice. The Parties shall then repeat the acceptance review process. If the deficiencies are not remediated after two (2) additional remediation cycles, Customer may escalate the matter pursuant to the dispute resolution procedures in Section 14.2 of the Agreement.
**EXHIBIT B**
**SERVICE LEVEL AGREEMENT AND SERVICE CREDIT SCHEDULE**

This Exhibit B is attached to and forms part of the AI Platform Agreement dated as of April 2, 2025 (the \"**Agreement**\"), between Meridian Cognitive Systems, LLC (\"**Vendor**\") and TechNova Solutions, Inc. (\"**Customer**\"). Capitalized terms used in this Exhibit B but not defined herein shall have the meanings ascribed to them in the Agreement. This Exhibit B sets forth the service level commitments applicable to the Platform and the service credit schedule applicable in the event of failure to meet such commitments, as referenced in Article 9 of the Agreement.
**1. Service Levels**
The following service level targets shall apply during the Term:
**Service Level**         **Target**        **Measurement Period**                                  **Measurement Methodology**
**Platform Uptime**       ≥ 99.9%           Calendar month                                          Vendor monitoring systems; calculated as ((Total Minutes − Downtime Minutes) / Total Minutes) × 100
**API Latency (p95)**     ≤ 600 ms          Calendar month                                          Vendor API gateway metrics; 95th percentile response time
**Model Accuracy (F1)**   ≥ 0.90            Per validation dataset review (no less than annually)   F1 score measured against mutually agreed validation dataset
**2. Scheduled Maintenance**

Vendor may schedule maintenance windows of up to four (4) hours per calendar month for the purpose of performing routine maintenance, upgrades, patches, and other operational activities on the Platform. Scheduled maintenance shall not be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA, provided that the following conditions are met:

> \(a\) Vendor provides Customer with at least forty-eight (48) hours\' prior written notice (via email to Customer\'s designated technical contact) of the scheduled maintenance window, specifying the date, start time, estimated duration, and nature of the maintenance activity;
> \(b\) Scheduled maintenance windows are scheduled during off-peak hours (between 12:00 AM and 6:00 AM Eastern Time, Saturday or Sunday) to the extent commercially practicable; and
> \(c\) The total duration of scheduled maintenance does not exceed four (4) hours in any single calendar month.

Maintenance that exceeds four (4) hours in any calendar month, or that is conducted without the requisite forty-eight (48) hours\' advance notice, shall be counted as Downtime for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
**3. Force Majeure Exclusion**
Downtime resulting from Force Majeure Events, as defined in Section 14.5 of the Agreement, shall be excluded from the calculation of Platform availability for purposes of the Uptime SLA.
**4. Service Credit Schedule --- Uptime Failures**

In the event Vendor fails to meet the Uptime SLA in any calendar month, Customer shall be entitled to a Service Credit calculated as a percentage of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment (\$200,000) for the affected calendar month, in accordance with the following tiered schedule:
**Monthly Uptime Achieved**         **Service Credit (% of Monthly Fee)**
**5. Service Credit Terms and Conditions**

> \(a\) **Request Requirement.** To receive a Service Credit, Customer must submit a written request to Vendor\'s support team within thirty (30) days following the end of the calendar month in which the Uptime SLA failure occurred. The request must identify the specific dates and times of the Downtime events and reference the applicable monthly service report. Vendor shall validate the claim against its monitoring data and notify Customer of the approved Service Credit amount within fifteen (15) business days of receipt of the request.

> \(b\) **Application of Credits.** Service Credits shall be applied as a credit against the next invoice(s) issued to Customer under the Agreement. Service Credits shall not be refundable in cash or any other form and may not be exchanged for other products, services, or consideration.

> \(c\) **Maximum Credits.** In no event shall the aggregate Service Credits issued to Customer in any single calendar month exceed twenty percent (20%) of the monthly Annual Platform Fee installment for such month (i.e., \$40,000). Service Credits shall not be carried forward beyond the then-current Contract Year. Upon expiration or termination of the Agreement, any unused Service Credits shall expire and shall not be refundable.

> \(d\) **Sole and Exclusive Remedy.** Service Credits constitute Customer\'s sole and exclusive remedy, and Vendor\'s sole and exclusive liability, for any failure to meet the Uptime SLA or any other service level commitment set forth in Article 9 of the Agreement or this Exhibit B.
**6. Latency and Accuracy**

No separate Service Credit mechanism is provided for failures to meet the API Latency (p95) or Model Accuracy (F1) targets set forth in Sections 9.2 and 9.3 of the Agreement. Vendor shall report on latency and accuracy performance in its monthly service reports as required by Section 9.5 of the Agreement. Persistent or material failures to meet the latency or accuracy targets shall be addressed through the Parties\' regular service review process and, if not resolved, may constitute a material breach of the Agreement subject to the termination provisions of Section 13.3.
*\[End of Exhibit B\]*
*\[End of Agreement\]*

**1. Scope.** This DPA applies to Vendor\'s processing of Customer Data as a service provider/processor on behalf of Customer.

Customer is the controller/business with respect to Customer Data. Vendor is the processor/service provider with respect to Customer Data and shall process Customer Data solely on behalf of Customer.

Vendor certifies that it is a \"service provider\" as defined in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag), and that it shall not sell, share, or retain Customer Data except as necessary to perform its obligations under the Agreement.
**4. GLBA Compliance**
Vendor acknowledges that Customer Data includes consumer NPPI subject to the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act and agrees to comply with all applicable safeguard requirements thereunder.
**5. Processing Instructions**
Vendor shall process Customer Data solely in accordance with Customer\'s documented instructions as set forth in the Agreement.
**6. Sub-Processor Requirements**

Vendor shall not engage any sub-processor to process Customer Data without Customer\'s prior written consent. Vendor shall impose data protection obligations on sub-processors that are no less protective than those set forth in this DPA and the Agreement. Vendor shall remain fully liable for the acts and omissions of its sub-processors.
**7. Data Security**

**Scripting XML Handling**

I'm diving into scriptwriting and need to handle XML namespaces and elements carefully. First, for accepted documents, I should find and remove any instances of w:ins/w:del. If they're nested in smart tags, that's something to consider. For text extraction, I want to focus on direct text, perhaps targeting paragraphs, but no need for extra line breaks.

I'm thinking about formatting issues too, like using track wrappers with w:r in w:del/ins. There are considerations for headings, possibly using bold via w:b, though that’s not crucial. Plus, I need to ensure that multi-paragraph provisions for sections are handled appropriately.

**Processing Document Changes**

I'm using a method to find paragraphs containing specific needles, especially after accepting documents, ensuring no duplicates from deletions. For replacements, old text will be matched with new strings. 

For renaming headings, like changing "Section 11.2 --- Vendor Remediation" to "Section 11.3 --- Vendor Remediation," I'll handle that. I also need to focus on paragraph replacements in sections 10.3 and 11.1 separately, ensuring proper numbering and checking for exact matches from currently parsed text. I'll also note that "API Latency (p95)" is a table cell, not a paragraph.

**Handling Table and Paragraphs**

I need to consider that some elements may be table cells, and my current search only looks for body paragraphs (w:p) without including nested tables. To include everything, I'll use a root.xpath('.//w:p') to get all paragraphs and table cells. For replacements, identifying the target by text is essential. I also want to focus on the paragraph around Exhibit B concerning the "Stabilization Period" and ensure I address content in Sections 6.1 and 6.2.

from zipfile import ZipFile, ZIP_DEFLATED
from lxml import etree
from copy import deepcopy
from pathlib import Path
from datetime import datetime, timezone

SRC = Path('documents/technova-ai-vendor-agreement-draft-2-redline.docx')
OUT = Path('output/draft-3-redline.docx')
W = 'http://schemas.openxmlformats.org/wordprocessingml/2006/main'
NS = {'w': W}
qn = lambda tag: f'{{{W}}}{tag}'


def accept_changes(root):
    # Accept all prior Draft 2 changes: remove deletions, unwrap insertions.
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for el in list(root.xpath('.//w:del', namespaces=NS)):
            parent = el.getparent()
            if parent is not None:
                parent.remove(el)
                changed = True
        for el in list(root.xpath('.//w:ins', namespaces=NS)):
            parent = el.getparent()
            if parent is not None:
                idx = parent.index(el)
                for child in list(el):
                    parent.insert(idx, child)
                    idx += 1
                parent.remove(el)
                changed = True
    return root


def ptext(p):
    return ''.join(p.xpath('.//w:t/text() | .//w:delText/text()', namespaces=NS))


def make_run(text, kind, bold=False, italic=False):
    r = etree.Element(qn('r'))
    rpr = etree.SubElement(r, qn('rPr'))
    color = etree.SubElement(rpr, qn('color'))
    color.set(qn('val'), 'C00000' if kind == 'del' else '0000FF')
    if kind == 'del':
        etree.SubElement(rpr, qn('strike'))
    else:
        u = etree.SubElement(rpr, qn('u'))
        u.set(qn('val'), 'single')
    if bold:
        etree.SubElement(rpr, qn('b'))
    if italic:
        etree.SubElement(rpr, qn('i'))
    t = etree.SubElement(r, qn('delText') if kind == 'del' else qn('t'))
    t.set('{http://www.w3.org/XML/1998/namespace}space', 'preserve')
    t.text = text
    return r


def tracked(p, old, new, heading=False):
    # Keep paragraph properties, replace all content with an explicit deletion/insertion pair.
    ppr = p.find(qn('pPr'))
    for child in list(p):
        if child is not ppr:
            p.remove(child)
    if old:
        d = etree.SubElement(p, qn('del'))
        d.set(qn('id'), '101')
        d.set(qn('author'), 'Kirkstead & Yao LLP')
        d.set(qn('date'), '2025-05-14T17:00:00Z')
        d.append(make_run(old, 'del', bold=heading))
    if new:
        ins = etree.SubElement(p, qn('ins'))
        ins.set(qn('id'), '102')
        ins.set(qn('author'), 'Kirkstead & Yao LLP')
        ins.set(qn('date'), '2025-05-14T17:00:00Z')
        ins.append(make_run(new, 'ins', bold=heading))


def find_paras(root, needle):
    return [p for p in root.xpath('.//w:p', namespaces=NS) if needle in ptext(p)]


def replace(root, needle, new, heading=False, occurrence=0):
    hits = find_paras(root, needle)
    if len(hits) <= occurrence:
        raise RuntimeError(f'Could not find occurrence {occurrence} of {needle!r}; got {len(hits)}')
    p = hits[occurrence]
    old = ptext(p)
    tracked(p, old, new, heading=heading)
    return p


def insert_after(root, needle, heading, body):
    hits = find_paras(root, needle)
    if not hits:
        raise RuntimeError(f'Could not find insertion anchor {needle!r}')
    anchor = hits[0]
    parent = anchor.getparent()
    idx = parent.index(anchor) + 1
    # use anchor paragraph properties as a reasonable visual match
    for text, is_heading in [(heading, True), (body, False)]:
        np = etree.Element(qn('p'))
        ppr = anchor.find(qn('pPr'))
        if ppr is not None:
            np.append(deepcopy(ppr))
        ins = etree.SubElement(np, qn('ins'))
        ins.set(qn('id'), '103' if is_heading else '104')
        ins.set(qn('author'), 'Kirkstead & Yao LLP')
        ins.set(qn('date'), '2025-05-14T17:00:00Z')
        ins.append(make_run(text, 'ins', bold=is_heading))
        parent.insert(idx, np)
        idx += 1

with ZipFile(SRC, 'r') as zin:

def tracked(p, old, new, heading=False):

lines.text: **Section 5A.1 --- Escrow Arrangement**

Within thirty (30) days of the Effective Date, Vendor shall enter into a three-party escrow agreement with Customer and Iron Mountain Intellectual Property Management, Inc. (the \"Escrow Agent\"), in a form reasonably satisfactory to Customer, pursuant to which Vendor shall deposit the Escrow Materials.
**Section 5A.2 --- Escrow Deposits**

[Vendor shall deposit and maintain current versions of the following Escrow Materials, and shall not be required to deposit the Base Model source code, Base Model weights, or Vendor\'s proprietary training infrastructure:]{.underline}
[The fine-tuned adapter weights comprising the Customer-Trained Adaptations, including each production version then deployed for Customer;]{.underline}

[All training configuration files and pipeline artifacts necessary to make the deposited adapter weights usable and to reproduce or redeploy the fine-tuned model, including hyperparameters, training scripts, preprocessing or feature-engineering scripts, inference and serving configuration, dependency specifications, and deployment documentation;]{.underline}
[Documentation and dependency information reasonably necessary to load, deploy, operate, and maintain the deposited adapter weights in connection with Customer\'s authorized use;]{.underline}
[A current manifest identifying third-party dependencies and license information to the extent necessary to use the deposited adapter weights;]{.underline}

[Vendor shall update the Escrow Materials within thirty (30) days following any material update to the deposited materials, and in any event no less frequently than quarterly. Each update shall correspond to the production adapter version then deployed for Customer and shall include the related configuration and pipeline artifacts.]{.underline}
**Section 5A.3 --- Release Conditions**
The Escrow Agent shall release the Escrow Materials to Customer upon the occurrence of any of the following release conditions:

[Vendor becomes subject to a voluntary or involuntary petition or proceeding for bankruptcy, insolvency, receivership, liquidation, dissolution, or similar relief, or makes an assignment for the benefit of creditors;]{.underline}
\(b\) Vendor commits a material breach of this Agreement that remains uncured for more than sixty (60) days after Customer\'s written notice specifying the breach;
[Vendor ceases to support, maintain, or make available the MeridianIQ Platform commercially, or publicly announces an end-of-life or discontinuation of product support.]{.underline}

Upon release, Customer shall receive a non-exclusive, irrevocable, perpetual, royalty-free, worldwide license to use, modify, compile, and deploy the Escrow Materials solely for Customer\'s internal business purposes in connection with LendStream.
**Section 5A.4 --- Escrow Costs**
Vendor shall bear all costs associated with establishing and maintaining the escrow arrangement, including Escrow Agent fees and deposit verification costs.
**Section 5A.5 --- Verification**

Customer shall have the right, no more than once per Contract Year, to request verification by the Escrow Agent or a mutually agreed third-party technical expert that the Escrow Materials are complete, current, and sufficient to build and deploy the Platform. Vendor shall cooperate with such verification. The cost of verification shall be borne by Customer, unless verification reveals a material deficiency, in which case Vendor shall bear the cost.\]
**[ARTICLE 6 --- DATA PROCESSING AND PRIVACY]{.underline}**
**Section 6.1 --- Customer Data Processing**

[Vendor shall process Customer Data solely to provide the Platform and perform Vendor\'s obligations under this Agreement. Vendor shall not sell, share, or use Customer Data, including any de-identified or aggregated form, to train, improve, benchmark, or develop any model, product, or service for Vendor or any third party unless: (a) the information meets the statutory de-identification standard in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m), including safeguards against re-identification and inadvertent release and a prohibition on any attempt to re-identify; and (b) the de-identification methodology and resulting data have been verified in writing by an independent third-party assessor approved in writing by Customer before any such use. This sentence is a specific contractual obligation and not merely a representation or warranty. Vendor shall not use any Customer Data for model improvement unless both conditions are satisfied.]{.underline}
**Section 6.2 --- \[DELETED: Controller\] \[ADDED: Service Provider / Processor\] Status**

[Vendor shall process Customer Data solely as a service provider (as defined in Cal. Civ. Code § 1798.140(ag)) and processor on behalf of Customer. Vendor shall not be deemed an independent controller or business with respect to any Customer Data. Vendor shall certify and comply with its service-provider status under the CCPA/CPRA in the Data Processing Addendum (Exhibit D), including the restrictions on sale, sharing, and retention, use, or disclosure outside the direct business relationship.]{.underline}
**Section 6.3 --- Compliance with Laws**

Each Party shall comply with all applicable data protection and privacy laws, rules, and regulations in connection with its processing of Customer Data under this Agreement, including without limitation: (a) the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, 15 U.S.C. §§ 6801--6809, and its implementing regulations, including Regulation S-P (17 C.F.R. Part 248) and the FTC Safeguards Rule (16 C.F.R. Part 314) (\"**GLBA**\"), to the extent applicable to the processing of NPPI; (b) the California Consumer Privacy Act of 2018, as amended by the California Privacy Rights Act of 2020, Cal. Civ. Code §§ 1798.100--1798.199.100 (\"**CCPA/CPRA**\"), to the extent applicable; and (c) any other applicable federal, state, or international data protection or privacy laws. Vendor\'s obligations as a service provider under CCPA/CPRA are further set forth in the Data Processing Addendum (Exhibit D).
**Section 6.4 --- Security Measures**

Vendor shall implement and maintain throughout the Term administrative, technical, and physical safeguards that are no less protective than industry-standard measures, including SOC 2 Type II controls, designed to protect Customer Data against unauthorized access, acquisition, use, disclosure, alteration, or destruction. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Vendor\'s security program shall include: (a) encryption of Customer Data in transit (using TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (using AES-256 or equivalent); (b) access controls, including multi-factor authentication, role-based access, and least-privilege principles; (c) regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing; (d) intrusion detection and prevention systems; (e) security incident response procedures; and (f) employee security awareness training. Vendor shall, upon Customer\'s reasonable request and no more than once per twelve (12)-month period, provide Customer with a summary of Vendor\'s then-current security measures and any SOC 2 Type II or equivalent audit reports covering Vendor\'s information security controls.
**Section 6.5 --- Data Breach Notification**
[notify Customer in writing within seventy-two (72) hours after Vendor first discovers or becomes aware of the Security Breach, without waiting for confirmation of its scope or cause]{.underline}
\[ADDED: \### Section 6.6 --- Sub-Processors

Vendor shall not engage any sub-processor to process Customer Data without Customer\'s prior written consent. Vendor shall maintain a list of sub-processors and provide such list to Customer upon request. Vendor shall impose data protection obligations on sub-processors that are no less protective than those set forth in this Agreement and the DPA. Vendor shall remain fully liable for the acts and omissions of its sub-processors.\]
**Section 6.\[DELETED: 6\] \[ADDED: 7\] --- Return and Deletion of Data**

Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, Vendor shall, at Customer\'s written election made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration, either (a) return Customer Data to Customer in a commercially reasonable format designated by Customer, or (b) securely delete or destroy all Customer Data in Vendor\'s possession or control, including all copies, backups, and archives thereof. Vendor shall complete such return or deletion within thirty (30) calendar days of receipt of Customer\'s written request. Upon completion of the return or deletion, Vendor shall certify in writing to Customer that all Customer Data has been returned or deleted in accordance with this Section 6. 7. Vendor shall not retain any Customer Data in any form following termination, except as required by applicable law, in which case Vendor shall (i) isolate such data, (ii) continue to protect it in accordance with this Agreement, and (iii) delete it as soon as the retention obligation expires. For the avoidance of doubt, no exception shall apply for de-identified or aggregated data, which shall also be returned or deleted upon Customer\'s request.
\[ADDED: \### Section 6.8 --- Data Processing Addendum

The Parties shall execute the Data Processing Addendum attached as Exhibit D contemporaneously with this Agreement. The DPA is incorporated into and forms part of this Agreement. In the event of any conflict between the DPA and this Agreement, the DPA shall control with respect to data protection matters.\]
**[ARTICLE 7 --- CONFIDENTIALITY]{.underline}**
**Section 7.1 --- Definition of Confidential Information**

\"**Confidential Information**\" means all non-public information disclosed by or on behalf of one Party (the \"**Disclosing Party**\") to the other Party (the \"**Receiving Party**\") in connection with this Agreement, whether disclosed orally, in writing, electronically, or by any other means, and whether or not marked or designated as \"confidential,\" \"proprietary,\" or with any similar legend, that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential given the nature of the information and the circumstances of disclosure. Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Confidential Information includes: (a) business plans, strategies, forecasts, and financial information; (b) technical information, including source code, algorithms, model architectures, model weights, training data, APIs, and system designs; (c) trade secrets; (d) customer lists, supplier lists, and pricing information; (e) product roadmaps and development plans; and (f) the terms and conditions of this Agreement, including all pricing, fee, and commercial terms. Customer Data shall be deemed Confidential Information of Customer regardless of whether it is marked or designated as confidential.

Confidential Information shall not include information that: (i) is or becomes publicly available through no fault of or breach by the Receiving Party; (ii) was already known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure by the Disclosing Party, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records; (iii) is rightfully received by the Receiving Party from a third party without restriction on disclosure and without breach of any obligation of confidentiality owed to the Disclosing Party; or (iv) is independently developed by the Receiving Party without use of or reference to the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information, as evidenced by the Receiving Party\'s written records.
**Section 7.2 --- Obligations**

The Receiving Party shall: (a) hold the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information in strict confidence; (b) not disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to any third party except as expressly permitted under Section 7.3; (c) use the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information solely for the purposes of performing its obligations or exercising its rights under this Agreement; and (d) protect the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information using measures that are no less protective than those used by the Receiving Party to protect its own most sensitive confidential information, but in no event less than a reasonable standard of care.

The confidentiality obligations set forth in this Article 7 shall remain in effect during the Term and for a period of five (5) years following the date of disclosure; provided, however, that the confidentiality obligations with respect to any Confidential Information that constitutes a trade secret under applicable law shall continue for so long as such information remains a trade secret.
**Section 7.3 --- Permitted Disclosures**

The Receiving Party may disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to its employees, officers, directors, agents, contractors, consultants, advisors, and Affiliates who have a legitimate need to know such information for the purposes of this Agreement and who are bound by written confidentiality obligations no less restrictive than those set forth in this Article 7 (collectively, \"**Authorized Recipients**\"). The Receiving Party shall be responsible for any breach of this Article 7 by its Authorized Recipients.

The Receiving Party may also disclose the Disclosing Party\'s Confidential Information to the extent required by applicable law, regulation, court order, subpoena, or other legal process, provided that the Receiving Party: (a) provides the Disclosing Party with prompt written notice of such requirement (to the extent legally permitted) so that the Disclosing Party may seek a protective order or other appropriate remedy; (b) cooperates with the Disclosing Party, at the Disclosing Party\'s expense, in seeking such protective order or other remedy; and (c) discloses only the minimum amount of Confidential Information necessary to comply with such requirement. Any Confidential Information disclosed pursuant to a legal compulsion shall retain its confidential status for all other purposes under this Agreement.
\[ADDED: \### Section 7.4 --- Injunctive Relief

Each Party acknowledges that a breach of this Article 7 may cause irreparable harm for which monetary damages would be an inadequate remedy. Accordingly, each Party shall be entitled to seek injunctive or other equitable relief from any court of competent jurisdiction without the necessity of proving actual damages or posting a bond or other security.\]

I want to check XML heading 5.2 for potential elements like w:delText. My acceptance function has removed w:del, but the text output shows `[DELETED`, possibly from w:t in w:ins. The parser from doc2 actually indicated both `[DELETED: Customer Data Ownership]` and `[ADDED: Customer Ownership...]`. It appears that the XML debug after the acceptance function shows similar findings, so I’m noting that down.

**Cleaning text markup**

I’m looking at a document that includes markers like `[ADDED:` and `\[DELETED:`. It seems like these are used intentionally to track changes, but they need to be cleaned up in the final version. When I accept changes, the inserted content shouldn't show these marker labels. 

I might consider building a function to strip these markers out of the text after accepting changes, but it's a bit risky since some paragraphs include literal wrapped text. Inspecting the raw XML for more clarity might be necessary.

replace(root, 'Vendor shall not engage any sub-processor to process Customer Data without Customer\'s prior written consent. Vendor shall provide at least thirty (30) days\' prior written notice of any proposed addition or replacement and shall not proceed without such consent. Vendor shall impose data protection obligations on sub-processors that are no less protective than those set forth in this DPA and the Agreement and shall remain fully liable for their acts and omissions.')
insert_after(root, 'Vendor shall assist Customer in responding to data subject requests, including requests for access, deletion, correction, and portability, to the extent applicable under CCPA/CPRA or other applicable law.', '10. Civ. Code § 1798.140(m), including safeguards against re-identification, processes preventing inadvertent release, and a prohibition on any attempt to re-identify. Before any such use, an independent third-party assessor approved in writing by Customer shall verify the de-identification methodology and resulting data in a written certification delivered to Customer. replace(root, '12. International Data Transfers', '13. International Data Transfers', heading=True)
replace(root, '13. Term.', '14. Term.', heading=True)

# SLA compromises and ramp."}

Without limiting the generality of the foregoing, Vendor\'s security program shall include: (a) encryption of Customer Data in transit (using TLS 1.2 or higher) and at rest (using AES-256 or equivalent); (b) access controls, including multi-factor authentication, role-based access, and least-privilege principles; (c) regular vulnerability assessments and penetration testing; (d) intrusion detection and prevention systems; (e) security incident response procedures; and (f) employee security awareness training. Vendor shall, upon Customer\'s reasonable request and no more than once per twelve (12)-month period, provide Customer with a summary of Vendor\'s then-current security measures and any SOC 2 Type II or equivalent audit reports covering Vendor\'s information security controls.
**Section 6.5 --- Data Breach Notification**

Section 6.6 --- Sub-Processors

Vendor shall not engage any sub-processor to process Customer Data without Customer\'s prior written consent. Vendor shall maintain a list of sub-processors and provide such list to Customer upon request. Vendor shall impose data protection obligations on sub-processors that are no less protective than those set forth in this Agreement and the DPA. Vendor shall remain fully liable for the acts and omissions of its sub-processors.
**Section 6.7 --- Return and Deletion of Data**

Upon termination or expiration of this Agreement, Vendor shall, at Customer\'s written election made within thirty (30) days following the effective date of termination or expiration, either (a) return Customer Data to Customer in a commercially reasonable format designated by Customer, or (b) securely delete or destroy all Customer Data in Vendor\'s possession or control, including all copies, backups, and archives thereof. Upon completion of the return or deletion, Vendor shall certify in writing to Customer that all Customer Data has been returned or deleted in accordance with this Section 6. 7. Vendor shall not retain any Customer Data in any form following termination, except as required by applicable law, in which case Vendor shall (i) isolate such data, (ii) continue to protect it in accordance with this Agreement, and (iii) delete it as soon as the retention obligation expires.
